events.text: The mouth of {sr_realm} is shaped like a body that struck the mountain and kept going. The stone around it has melted and set again in ripples, like wax. Even here the qi is so thick it stings the throat, and the first line of carved script, at the height of a tall man's hand, glows when you breathe on it.

choices.text: Breathe slowly and let the air settle in you

effects.log: You take the cave's air a sip at a time. By the tenth breath your meridians stop burning and start to drink.

choices.text: Read the glowing line

effects.log: It says only: "Mind the step." You look down. The floor drops away an arm's length ahead, hidden by the glare.

choices.text: Push in before the others crowd the passage

effects.log: You are first through. Behind you the passage fills with elbows and curses, and you are already out of sight.

events.text: A few hundred paces in, the dust stops falling. It hangs in the lantern light, every mote still, as if the cave were holding its breath since the day the immortal landed. Your own steps leave holes in the hanging cloud that do not close behind you.

choices.text: Walk through it carefully, disturbing as little as you can

effects.log: You move like a thief through a sleeping house. The dust closes behind you after all, slowly, as if it approved.

choices.text: Catch a mote between two fingers

effects.log: It is warm, and heavier than it looks. When you open your fingers it has become a speck of gold leaf.

choices.text: Blow through it and watch the patterns

effects.log: Your breath makes a shape in the still dust that looks, for a moment, like a falling figure. Then the cloud is only dust again.

events.text: {sr_sect} came in force. At the first junction the party's leader draws a map in the dust with the butt of a spear, divides the cave into three, and gives the deepest third to the youngest because "they have the least to lose". You can feel everyone counting how much each of the others has to lose.

choices.text: Offer to take the deep third yourself

effects.log: The leader looks at you a long moment, then nods. The young ones are sent to the shallow halls. Several of them will remember this.

choices.text: Keep your head down and follow the plan

effects.log: You go where you are told. Nobody thanks you, and nobody blames you either, which in a sect is a kind of peace.

choices.text: Quietly mark the walls so the young can find their way back

effects.log: You scratch small arrows at every turn. Later, in the dark, three of them follow your marks home.

events.text: The crack you came through was not made by the immortal. Someone chiselled it, long ago, a hand's width at a time; the tool marks are still crisp. Halfway along, wedged into the rock, is a thief's bundle: a rusted chisel, a dry flask, and a note that reads, "Third opening. I will get it this time."

choices.text: Leave the bundle where it is

effects.log: Whoever it was meant to come back for it. You squeeze past and leave the past its property.

choices.text: Take the chisel; it still has an edge

effects.log: It is better steel than it looks. You will find a use for it before the day is out.

choices.text: Add a line to the note

effects.log: You write: "Fourth opening. Someone got this far for you." It feels like the right thing to leave in a crack in a mountain.

events.text: You know this cave. Not the way you know a story; the way your hands know a door at night. The third step down is loose. The wall on the left is warm, the right cold. Somewhere deeper, a line of script you once traced with a finger is waiting to be traced again, and you could walk to it with your eyes shut.

choices.text: Walk to it with your eyes shut

effects.log: You do. Your fingertips find the carved line exactly where they expected, worn a little smoother than the rest. By a past you.

choices.text: Take another way, to see what that life missed

effects.log: You turn down a passage the old memory never chose. It is narrower, and it opens on a small hall nobody has touched.

choices.text: Stop and let the memory finish

effects.log: You stand in the dark until the other life's footsteps fade out of your own. It walked faster than you do. It was in a hurry.

events.text: There is a hollow in the wall at the bend before the long stair, about the size of a crouching body. You know it at once, with a cold that has nothing to do with the cave. Somebody you used to be crawled in here near the end. On the stone, scratched by a fingernail, are four strokes of a name you no longer carry.

choices.text: Kneel and finish the name

effects.log: You add the last strokes. It is your old name, now complete, and the hollow is only a hollow afterward.

choices.text: Sit in the hollow a moment

effects.log: It fits you badly. That body was taller. You sit anyway, and say aloud that you came back. It helps more than you thought it would.

choices.text: Walk past without looking

effects.log: You walk past. Your hands shake for a hundred paces and then stop, and you are proud of that, a little.

events.text: The young ones at the barrier stared when you came through, as if it were strange for anyone your age to want anything. Inside, the cave's rich qi finds every stiff joint you own and fills it like warm water. For the first time in years your knees do not ache on a stair.

choices.text: Climb the long stair just because you can

effects.log: You take the stair two at a time, the way you have not in decades. At the top you laugh out loud, alone, and the cave laughs back.

choices.text: Sit and let the qi do its work

effects.log: You sit for the length of a meal. When you stand, the old wound in your side has stopped talking.

choices.text: Tell the young ones to save their breath

effects.log: They roll their eyes. Two of them, later, will save it exactly when you said, and live.

events.text: The barrier almost does not let you through. It holds you a moment, like a hand on a collar, and then releases you with what feels very much like doubt. Deeper in, something huge turns its attention your way and decides, for now, you are not worth getting up for.

choices.text: Be glad of it and stay small

effects.log: You move quietly and touch nothing that looks important. Being beneath notice is a skill, and today you are a master of it.

choices.text: Make yourself worth getting up for

effects.log: You train in the first empty hall until your arms burn. The attention comes back, briefly, curious.

choices.text: Ask the walls what to do

effects.log: The nearest carving glows: "Be honest about your size, and the cave will be honest about its doors." You find a low door you would have missed.

events.text: You have walked into secret realms before, and you thought you knew their feel: the cold of the barrier, the held breath, the greed of everyone around you. This one is different. It is not a place that was made. It is a place that happened, the way a scar happens, and it still remembers the hurt.

choices.text: Treat it like a wound, gently

effects.log: You step soft and speak low. The others look at you strangely, then start to do the same.

choices.text: Use what the other realms taught you

effects.log: You read the airflow, the dust, the tilt of the floor. The cave gives up two of its easier secrets without a fight.

events.text: A disciple of your party catches up with you on the stair, out of breath, and asks the question the young always ask in this cave: "Was the immortal a good person, Elder? Or a criminal?" Everyone in earshot goes quiet to hear what an elder will say.

choices.text: "A criminal, by Heaven's law. Good, by mine."

effects.log: The disciple turns this over all the way down the stair. Some of the others look at you differently afterward.

choices.text: "Read the walls and decide for yourself."

effects.log: They do, and argue about it for the rest of the expedition. That is the best thing an elder can start.

choices.text: "Neither. A person who fell."

effects.log: It is not the answer they wanted. Years later one of them will repeat it, word for word, to their own disciple.

events.text: Halfway down the long stair, under the immortal's first letter, there is another line, cut in a rougher hand. You know it before you have read it, because you wrote it, in a life that ended long ago. And under your line, smaller still, somebody else has answered you.

choices.text: Read their answer

effects.log: "I read yours, and went on. Thank you." No name. You run your thumb over the strokes and climb on, lighter.

choices.text: Add one more line beneath theirs

effects.log: You cut a single word. It is not for the immortal anymore; it is for whoever comes next.

events.text: An old woman sits on a pack at the cave mouth, so small and still the crowd parts around her like water round a stone. She is Gong Ha-rim, she tells you, and she is one hundred and forty. "My teacher died at the trial when I was twenty. At eighty I came back and lost my nerve at the stair. This is my last opening. Will you walk me to his bones?"

choices.text: Offer her your arm

effects.log: She takes it with a grip like a hawk's. "Ju Pyeong," she says. "That was his name. Say it if you find him first."

choices.text: Promise to bring the bones out to her

effects.log: "He wore a jade pin like a pine tree," she says, and sits back down on her pack to wait. "I have waited a hundred and twenty years. I can wait a day."

choices.text: Tell her the cave is no place for her

effects.log: She smiles without arguing, which is worse than arguing. When you look back from the first turn, the pack is still there and she is not.

events.text: Ha-rim walks slower than anyone in the cave and somehow never falls behind. She talks the whole way, about Ju Pyeong: how he burned rice, how he sang off key, how he once carried her across a river in flood and complained about it for a year. At a fork she taps the wall without looking. "Left. He told me, before he went in."

choices.text: Take her left

effects.log: The left passage is dry and quiet, and at its end a niche holds an old lantern with a pine carved on it. "His," she says, and her voice breaks on it.

choices.text: Ask why he went in at all

effects.log: "For me," she says simply. "I was dying of a cough. He thought the immortal's art could cure it. I got better on my own, a month later."

choices.text: Carry her up the next stair

effects.log: She weighs less than a sack of rice and complains the whole way, exactly the way she said he did. You are both laughing at the top.

events.text: Deep in, among the bones of animals and the dropped packs of other openings, you keep looking for a jade pine. You turn over a dozen skeletons of beasts and two of people, neither with a pin. Your promise sits in your chest like a stone you swallowed. A hundred and twenty years is a long time to wait for someone to keep a promise.

choices.text: Search the side halls, even if it costs you time

effects.log: You lose an hour and skin your knuckles, and in the last hall you find a scrap of blue cloth with a pine stitched on it. You are close.

choices.text: Go on toward the trial; that is where he died

effects.log: You go straight on. The stone of your promise grows heavier with every step closer to the trial hall.

events.text: Two halls in you find her, sitting on the bottom step of the long stair with her eyes closed, breathing in short hard pulls. She came in after all, alone, the moment you looked away. "Just resting," she says, without opening her eyes. "Go on. I know the way. He told me."

choices.text: Pick her up and take her with you

effects.log: She does not argue this time. You carry her up the stair on your back, and she directs you like a general from behind your ear.

choices.text: Leave her a flask and go on

effects.log: She takes the flask and nods you on. When you glance back from the top of the stair, she has begun to climb, one step at a time.

events.text: When the trial is over, the hall is very quiet, and in the far corner, beside the platform where the shadow stood, lies what is left of Ju Pyeong: bones gone yellow as old paper, a broken sword, a jade hairpin shaped like a pine. He died facing the shadow, not running. His hand is still reaching for the door, toward the way out, toward her.

choices.text: Wrap the bones in your outer robe to carry out

effects.log: You fold him into the cloth as carefully as you can. He is very light. You understand now how she has carried him all these years.

choices.text: Take only the hairpin

effects.log: It is warm from the cave. You tuck it into your collar, and it feels, ridiculously, like being trusted.

events.text: You are on the floor of the trial hall, with the shadow standing over you, when a small old woman walks straight past it as if it were furniture. Ha-rim kneels in the far corner beside a heap of yellow bones and a pine-shaped pin. The shadow watches her and does not strike. It seems the trial does not raise a hand against the old who come for their dead.

choices.text: Crawl over and help her gather him

effects.log: You gather Ju Pyeong together, the two of you, while the immortal's shadow stands guard over the door like a mourner.

choices.text: Watch, and let her have this alone

effects.log: She talks to the bones in a low voice for a long time. You do not listen. When she stands, she is carrying him herself.

events.text: After the trial, when you can see again, you find Ha-rim in the corner of the hall. She made it on her own. She is sitting against the wall beside a heap of yellow bones, one hand resting on them, her head tipped back as if listening to music. She has gone, quietly, in the one place she wanted to be. Her face is younger than it was at the door.

choices.text: Leave them together, and close the corner off with stones

effects.log: You build a small cairn over the two of them. It is the only grave in the whole cave, and the shadow, you notice, does not walk near it.

choices.text: Carry them both out to be buried in the sun

effects.log: They are lighter together than you expected. You carry them out the way you would carry two sleeping children.

events.text: From where you lie, beaten, you can see the far corner of the trial hall: yellow bones, a broken sword, a glint of green that might be a jade pine. Twenty paces. The shadow stands between you and them and will not move for someone it has just put on the floor. You promised an old woman at the door.

choices.text: Crawl for it anyway

effects.log: You get eleven paces before the shadow sets you gently back where you started. Twice. You stop when you can no longer lift your arms.

choices.text: Fix the place in your memory, for her

effects.log: You learn the corner by heart: the angle of the bones, the crack in the wall above them. She will want to know.

events.text: Ha-rim is still sitting on her pack at the gate, exactly where you left her, as if she had not moved all day. She sees your empty hands from a long way off. By the time you reach her she has already decided to make it easy for you. "Well," she says. "Did you see him, at least?"

choices.text: Tell her everything you saw, exactly

effects.log: You describe the corner, the pin, the hand reaching for the door. She listens with her eyes closed. "Toward the door," she repeats. "Of course he was."

choices.text: Promise to come back at the next opening

effects.log: "In sixty years?" She laughs until she coughs. "Bring him to my grave, then. I will be the one under the pine by the road."

events.text: There is a pine by the road to {sr_realm}, old and crooked, with a grave under it that somebody keeps tidy. You stop before you know why. Then you remember: an old woman on a pack, a promise to bring a teacher's bones out to her grave. That was another life. The promise, it seems, came along anyway.

choices.text: Swear to the grave you will bring him this time

effects.log: You say it aloud to the pine. A needle falls on your sleeve, which is as close to an answer as a grave can give.

choices.text: Leave a cup of tea and go in

effects.log: You pour it into the roots. "Ju Pyeong," you say, so she will hear the name. Then you go into the cave to look for him.

events.text: At the gate, under an ordinary sky, you set Ju Pyeong down in the grass. If Ha-rim is still with you she sits beside him and says nothing for a long time; if not, the wind does the talking. Before the crowds come out behind you, someone has to decide what becomes of a teacher who went into a cave for a cough.

choices.text: Bury him under the pine by the road

effects.log: It takes the rest of the day. The pine has a jade-green tinge to it after, or you imagine it. People will call it the Waiting Pine.

choices.text: Take him to his old hall, wherever it stands

effects.log: You ask around and find it: a ruin with one disciple left, who weeps when you bring him home and gives you a page of the old art in thanks.

choices.text: Let the hermit choose, if she is here to choose

effects.log: If she lives, she chooses a hill facing the river he carried her across. If not, you choose it for her. It is the same hill either way.

events.text: A young man in grey with three small bronze bells at his belt plants himself in your path. "Yu Seon-gak, of the Nine Bells Hall." There were nine bells once; you can count how many are left. "My hall needs that legacy more than yours needs anything. So: whoever reaches the trial first, the other stands aside. Agreed?"

choices.text: Agree to the race

effects.log: "Good." He is off before the word is finished, bells chiming down the passage. He did not wait to hear whether you would cheat.

choices.text: Offer to go together and settle it at the trial

effects.log: He hesitates, suspicious of kindness. "Together, then. But I will not owe you." He owes you already, and you both know it.

choices.text: Laugh and step around him

effects.log: His face goes red to the ears. "You will remember my name," he says, which is what everyone says before they are forgotten.

events.arc: The Heir Who Was Not Chosen

events.text: The floor of the scripted hall gives way, letter by letter, as if the words were bored with holding anyone up. Ahead of you Yu Seon-gak drops to the waist in falling stone and grabs the edge, and his bells ring like a warning. Whatever you agreed at the mouth, he is looking at you now the way people look at a rope.

choices.text: Haul him out, whatever it costs

effects.log: The edge cuts your palms. He comes out grey with dust and shaking, and does not say thank you, because he cannot yet.

choices.text: Find the line of script that holds the floor and press it

ok.log: You read the hall in one long look, find the one word still bearing weight, and lean on it. The floor stops. Yu climbs out on his own, staring at you.

fail.log: You press the wrong word and the floor drops another foot. You haul him out by the collar after all, scraped raw.

choices.text: Step around the hole and go on

effects.log: His bells ring behind you for a long time, and then they stop. You tell yourself he climbed out. You will tell yourself that often.

events.arc: The Heir Who Was Not Chosen

events.text: Yu Seon-gak comes into the trial hall as the shadow fades, and stops dead at what lies beyond it: the immortal's legacy, waiting for you, not for him. He was the best of a dying hall, and he has just learned there is someone better. "May I touch it?" he asks, and hates himself for asking. "Just once. So I can say I did."

choices.text: Let him hold it as long as he likes

effects.log: He holds it with both hands and his eyes closed. When he gives it back, something proud in him has gone quiet, and something steadier has come instead.

choices.text: Teach him the one move you learned from the shadow

effects.log: You show him the step. He learns it in three tries, faster than you did. "Now my hall has one bell more," he says.

choices.text: Tell him no; it chose you

effects.log: He nods stiffly. You were right, and it costs nothing, and you will think about his face for years.

events.arc: The Heir Who Was Not Chosen

events.text: The shadow's hand is coming down for the last time when three bronze bells ring behind it. Yu Seon-gak hits it from the side with everything the Nine Bells Hall ever taught, which is not enough to beat it and is just enough to make it turn. He drags you out of the circle by your belt. "Now," he pants, "we are even."

choices.text: Tell him you are not even; you owe him

effects.log: "Good," he says, and grins for the first time since the mouth of the cave. "I like being owed."

choices.text: Ask him to try the trial himself, now that it is tired

effects.log: He looks at the shadow, then at you, and shakes his head. "Not today. Today I am the one who pulled someone out." It seems to be enough for him.

events.arc: The Heir Who Was Not Chosen

events.text: At the edge of the trial hall, on the floor, lies one small bronze bell, its cord snapped. Nobody else came this way. Whatever happened to Yu Seon-gak after the floor gave way, he got as far as this, or the bell did. It rings once when you nudge it with your foot, a thin clear note that does not fade the way a note should.

choices.text: Carry the bell out to his hall

effects.log: It rings with every step, all the way to the gate. You will have to find the Nine Bells Hall and say what you did not do.

choices.text: Leave it where it fell

effects.log: You leave it. Its note follows you a long way into the cave, and then stops, the way the others did.

events.arc: The Heir Who Was Not Chosen

events.text: At the closing gate the elders of the Nine Bells Hall are waiting, four old people in grey with no bells left at all. Yu Seon-gak walks out empty-handed beside you, and you watch him get smaller with every step toward them. The whole hall's hope came in with him this morning.

choices.text: Tell them he saved your life

effects.log: You say it loudly, in front of everyone. The elders look at him as if seeing him for the first time. One of them takes off his own robe and puts it on Yu's shoulders.

choices.text: Give him something from the cave

effects.log: You press a handful of what you carried into his hands. He tries to refuse and cannot, and the elders bow to you, very low.

choices.text: Say nothing; it is his hall, and his walk

effects.log: He walks the last stretch alone, straight-backed. Whatever he tells them, it is his to tell. Years later you hear the Nine Bells Hall has four bells again.

events.arc: The Heir Who Was Not Chosen

events.text: You come out of the gate with a small bronze bell in your hand, and a boy in grey at the edge of the crowd sees it and goes white. He runs. A little later four old people in grey come through the crowd toward you, slowly, already knowing.

choices.text: Tell them the truth

effects.log: You tell them about the floor and the rope you did not throw. They listen to the end. The eldest takes the bell and says, "Thank you for not lying." It is worse than a curse.

choices.text: Tell them he died bravely at the trial

effects.log: They bow and thank you, and weep, and take the bell. The lie sits easy for a year, and then it does not.

events.arc: The Heir Who Was Not Chosen

events.text: The script on the walls is not decoration. Close up, the lines are letters, cut by a fingertip into living rock, and the first is signed: Baek Ryeon-ha. "To whoever comes in. They will tell you I was thrown out of Heaven. I was not. I jumped, and I would do it again. Read on if you want to know why."

choices.text: Read on

effects.log: You follow the letters down the passage like footprints. The immortal's hand is steady and a little impatient, like someone who knew they had a long time and not enough.

choices.text: Copy the first letter onto a scrap of cloth

effects.log: It takes an hour. The cloth grows warm as you write. When you finish, the words on it glow faintly too.

events.text: The second letter runs the whole length of a gallery, its strokes deeper where he was angry. "There was a village under my mountain. A river was going to drown it on a day Heaven had written down. I was told to watch. I turned the river with one hand instead, and three hundred people woke up the next morning and never knew they should not have."

choices.text: Lay your hand where his hand was

effects.log: The stone fits your palm. For a heartbeat you feel a river, enormous, turning aside like a startled horse.

choices.text: Ask the wall whether it was worth it

effects.log: The next line answers you, as if he expected the question: "Ask me at the end."

events.text: As the shadow of the immortal fades, it does a thing the stories never mention: it speaks. Its voice is the voice of the letters. "Three hundred people," it says. "Their grandchildren's grandchildren are out there now, thousands of them. You are probably one." It bows to you, an immortal's bow, very slight and very deep.

choices.text: Bow back, as low as you can

effects.log: You bow until your forehead touches the warm floor. When you rise the shadow is gone, and the hall smells of river water.

choices.text: Ask it the question now: was it worth it?

effects.log: It looks at you for a long time. "You are standing here," it says, and fades. You decide that is a yes.

events.text: You are on your back on the trial floor, and the shadow of the immortal kneels beside you instead of striking. "I fell too," it says, in the voice of the letters. "Further than you. Get up when you can. There is one more letter, at the gate, and I wrote it for people who lost to me."

choices.text: Get up

effects.log: It takes three tries. The shadow waits through all of them without helping, which turns out to be a kind of help.

choices.text: Ask it why it fights at all

effects.log: "So that whoever takes what I know has fallen first," it says. "Heaven never fell. That was its whole trouble."

events.text: The last letter is cut into the inside of the gate itself, where only someone leaving would see it. "Carry nothing of mine out except this: it was worth it. Every year down here was worth it. If Heaven ever asks you to stand and watch, I hope you remember a cave." Beneath it the stone is smooth, as if waiting for an answer.

choices.text: Cut your answer into the stone

effects.log: You carve one line with the edge of your blade. You do not tell anyone what it says. It will be there long after you.

choices.text: Learn the letter by heart and carry it out

effects.log: You say it to yourself all the way out of the gate. Years later you will say it to someone who needs it.

choices.text: Tell the crowd outside the whole story

effects.log: By nightfall half the people at the gate know about the river and the three hundred. By next year it is a song.

events.text: The road down runs through galleries of script, wall after wall of it, and somewhere in the middle of the third gallery you realise the letters are getting smaller and more crowded, as if whoever carved them was running out of room, or time, or both.

choices.text: Read a little as you walk

effects.log: Most of it is the plain thinking of a mind with too much time: on rain, on rice, on the right way to fold a sleeve. One line on breathing is worth the whole walk.

choices.text: Keep your eyes on the floor and move

effects.log: You make good time and miss everything. At the end of the gallery a pack of other entrants is still reading, far behind you.

events.text: The road crosses a hall with a perfectly round well in the middle, its water so still and clear you can see a heap of old coins at the bottom, forty feet down. Every person who passes seems to have thrown one in. There is a small stack of fresh coins on the rim, left by somebody for whoever had none.

choices.text: Throw in a coin of your own

effects.log: It falls a long time without a ripple. You feel foolish and lucky at once.

choices.text: Add to the stack on the rim

effects.log: You leave three coins for the next person who has none. It is a small thing to leave in a great realm.

choices.text: Drink from the well

effects.log: It tastes of stone and something brighter underneath. Your head clears like a sky after rain.

events.text: The safe road is crowded with other parties, all keeping a careful distance, all pretending not to watch each other. At a narrow ledge two rival groups meet head on, and for a moment it looks as if blood will come of who goes first.

choices.text: Step back and wave both through

effects.log: Both groups eye you suspiciously, then pass. You lose a little time and gain two parties who will not ambush you later.

choices.text: Go first while they argue

effects.log: You slip across the ledge while they shout at each other. By the time they notice, you are gone.

choices.text: Talk them into going together

ok.log: You make a joke, then a suggestion. Somehow both groups cross side by side, grumbling, and one of them shares their water with you after.

fail.log: They both turn on you for interfering. You cross last, with a bruise and no friends.

events.text: The beast road runs through the cave's deep places, where things have lived for three thousand years on the immortal's leftover qi. The worst are the stone salamanders, long as boats, which do not bite: they lean on you, and drink your qi through your skin like water through cloth.

choices.text: Burn your qi hot so they let go

effects.log: You flare like a torch. They drop off with a hiss, and you stagger on, light-headed and empty.

choices.text: Let one drink, and read it while it does

effects.log: For a long moment you and the salamander share a single slow pulse. Then it lets go, satisfied, and you understand something about stillness.

choices.text: Run, and leave your pack as a decoy

effects.log: They swarm the pack and you get clear. Whatever was in it, the cave has it now.

events.text: Off the beast road, behind a curtain of hanging roots, is a den with no beast in it, only a bed of old moulted salamander skins, each as clear and hard as glass. Healers pay well for these, and armourers pay better.

choices.text: Take as many as you can carry

effects.log: You load yourself until you clink. The den watches you go with something like disapproval.

choices.text: Take one, and leave the rest

effects.log: One skin, wrapped in your sleeve. Something in the dark beyond the roots relaxes.

events.text: Your feet turn off the road at a blank wall, and your hand presses a carved stroke that is not quite like the others, and the wall swings in like a door. The memory did not come as a picture. It came as a habit, the way you might reach for a cup that was always on the left of the table.

choices.text: Go through, and close it behind you

effects.log: The hidden road is dry and quiet and lit by the glow of the script. Nobody else will find this way today. Nobody has since you.

choices.text: Leave it open for whoever is behind you

effects.log: A minute later you hear surprised voices, and then grateful ones. Whoever they are, they will have a better day than they expected.

events.text: Halfway along the hidden road there is a niche with a flat stone over it, and on the stone, scratched small, a mark you have never seen before in this life and know at once: your own mark, from before. Under the stone are things a past you hid for a future you, in the confident handwriting of someone sure you would come.

choices.text: Take what you left

effects.log: A pouch of old silver, a page of notes in your old hand. You read the notes and laugh: you were wrong about half of it, and the other half is gold.

choices.text: Take it, and leave something for the next life

effects.log: You put back a page of your own notes, and your own mark, freshly scratched. Whoever you are next will laugh at it too.

events.text: The road takes you past the place where a past life died. You did not come for it. Your feet just go there, the way a tongue goes to a missing tooth. There is nothing to see: a patch of wall, a stretch of floor. Then you notice the floor has been swept, recently, by somebody.

choices.text: Sweep it again yourself

effects.log: You sweep it with your sleeve until the stone shines. You do not know who else does this. You hope they come back.

choices.text: Wait to see who comes to sweep it

effects.log: Nobody comes. When you leave, you find a broom propped by the passage that was not there before.

events.text: The others on the road are faster than you, and it does not matter, because the cave keeps slowing the young: it wants patience, and you have more of that than anyone here. By the trial hall you have passed half of them, sitting with their heads in their hands.

choices.text: Tell them what the walls are for

effects.log: "Read them. Slowly." Two of them do. One of them looks up at you an hour later as if you were the immortal yourself.

choices.text: Pass them in silence

effects.log: You leave them to learn it the hard way. It is how you learned it.

events.text: When it is over, the trial hall goes still, and the dust begins to fall again for the first time since you came in. You notice there are new lines carved on the floor of the platform, lines that were not there a moment ago, fresh as if someone had just lifted a finger from the stone.

choices.text: Read what it wrote about you

effects.log: It is one sentence, and fair, and not entirely kind. You commit it to memory anyway.

choices.text: Rub them out with your sleeve

effects.log: They will not rub out. The cave keeps what it learns. You leave with the uncomfortable feeling of having been written down.

events.text: You sit on the edge of the trial platform to get your breath back. Across the hall, other entrants are only now arriving, wide-eyed, and you can see in their faces what you must look like: someone who has stood in front of a piece of Heaven and is still here.

choices.text: Warn them what it does

effects.log: You tell them how it moves, where it waits, what it wants. Some of them listen. You will never know which of them it saved.

choices.text: Say nothing and let them find out

effects.log: Everyone should meet it fresh, you decide. That is the trial. They walk in past you, and you do not watch.

events.text: The shadow of the immortal fights with an art three thousand years old, slower than you expected and impossible to get past, like trying to push through a river. You beat it by doing the one thing it did not teach: you stopped trying to win, and stood still. It stopped too. Then it stepped aside.

choices.text: Hold the stillness a moment longer

effects.log: In the stillness you understand one move of its art, completely, the way you understand your own hand.

choices.text: Go straight to the legacy

effects.log: It is not a scroll, or a weapon. It is a warmth in the chest, settling like a cat that has finally chosen a lap.

events.text: You beat the shadow of the immortal, barely, at the cost of everything you had. It falls to one knee on the platform and looks up at you with mild surprise, the expression of a teacher whose slowest student has finally done the sum. "Again," it says, "in another life, and you will do it better."

choices.text: Promise it you will

effects.log: It nods, and folds itself into the stone, and the legacy waits behind where it was. You feel the promise settle into your soul like a seed.

choices.text: Help it to its feet

effects.log: Your hand passes through it, of course. But it smiles at the gesture as it fades, and the hall warms.

events.text: The shadow beats you the way rain beats a field: without anger, without hurry, completely. When you are down it does not strike again. It simply waits, standing over you, until you understand you have been weighed and found not ready, and that it is not ashamed of you for that.

choices.text: Ask it what you lacked

effects.log: It touches two fingers to your chest, then to your forehead. The first touch hurts more.

choices.text: Crawl out with what dignity you have left

effects.log: You crawl out. It is a long hall. Halfway across you get up and walk, and you hear, or think you hear, something like approval.

events.text: You lie on the cave floor with the taste of iron in your mouth and watch the shadow return to its place on the platform. Behind it the immortal's legacy glows, close enough to reach, if you could stand. A carving on the floor beside your face reads, in letters smaller than the rest: "Most of them lie here a while."

choices.text: Lie here a while

effects.log: You lie still and breathe until the cave's qi has mended what it can. It is strange to be comforted by a floor.

choices.text: Get up now, out of pride

effects.log: You stand. It costs you. The shadow tilts its head, the way you might at a child who will not admit they are tired.

events.text: You go past the shadow of the immortal by not being worth its notice, which is harder than it sounds: you empty your intent, your greed, even your fear, until you are as uninteresting as a stone. It turns its blank face toward you once and turns away. The legacy is beyond your reach now, but you are through.

choices.text: Keep the emptiness as long as you can

effects.log: Long after you are past, you hold it. When it finally goes, you know you can find it again.

choices.text: Look back at it once you are safe

effects.log: It is looking at you too. It lifts one hand, slightly, the salute between two people who both know what just happened.

events.text: You try to slip along the wall of the trial hall, and the shadow is simply there in front of you, without having moved. It does not strike hard. It taps you, once, on the breastbone, and you fly back across the hall the way a child's ball flies, and land the same way.

choices.text: Laugh, because it was fair

effects.log: It was. You laugh lying on the floor, and the shadow, you swear, almost smiles.

choices.text: Try once more, slower

effects.log: You get two steps further. It taps you again. You have learned exactly how far two steps are, and that is something.

events.text: The shadow of the immortal killed someone you used to be. You remember it now, the moment you see it: the hand coming down, the cold floor. This time you are still standing at the end, and it is the one on its knee. It looks at you as if it, too, remembers.

choices.text: Say: "I came back."

effects.log: "I know," it says. "They always do, the ones worth killing." It bows, and goes into the stone.

choices.text: Say nothing; it was a fair fight both times

effects.log: You leave it the dignity of silence. The legacy, when you touch it, feels like a debt paid in full.

events.text: By every measure you should not have won. The shadow knows it too. It stands on the platform with its head tilted, examining you as if you were a sum that came out wrong. Then it laughs, an old person's laugh, delighted, and claps its translucent hands once.

choices.text: Bow, and admit you were lucky

effects.log: "Luck is a part of the art," it says, "the part nobody can teach." It gives you a little extra, like a grandparent.

choices.text: Tell it you were not lucky, just stubborn

effects.log: "Stubborn is the other part," it agrees, and steps aside.

events.text: Behind you {sr_realm} closes the way a wound closes, from the inside out, in a long slow shudder. The melted stone around the mouth runs and sets again. For a moment the mountain is whole, a mountain like any other, and then the scar shows through again, faint, waiting sixty years.

choices.text: Watch it seal all the way

effects.log: You watch until the last glow goes out. It feels like seeing someone off at a ferry.

choices.text: Walk away without looking back

effects.log: You have what you have. The cave has what it has. It seems a fair division.

events.text: Outside the gate the crowd is enormous: families, sect elders, merchants with scales already set up, and the quiet ones who come to see who does not come out. People look at your face first and your hands second, trying to read what you found.

choices.text: Give them nothing to read

effects.log: You walk through them with an empty face and empty hands, and by the time they start to whisper you are gone.

choices.text: Find someone waiting for a person who did not come out

effects.log: There is always one. You sit with them a while, and tell them what the cave was like inside. It helps them, a little.

events.text: At the gate you hand over {sr_treasure} to {sr_sect}, as the party agreed. The elders handle it reverently, like a thing that might break or might bite. One of them, an old woman who came in sixty years ago and found nothing, holds it a long time before she passes it on.

choices.text: Tell them how you won it

effects.log: They listen in silence. Some of what you say will be written into the hall's records, under your name.

choices.text: Ask the old elder what she remembers of her opening

effects.log: She tells you about a stair she was too afraid to climb. "You climbed it," she says. "Good." It means more than the payment.

events.text: You keep {sr_treasure} for yourself. It sits under your ribs like a second, slower heart. On the road out, three different people try to buy it from you with their eyes, and one with actual silver, and you tell all of them the same thing, which is nothing.

choices.text: Go somewhere quiet and let it settle

effects.log: You find a hut and sit for three days. When you come out, you move like water finding its level.

choices.text: Go straight home by the busy road

effects.log: You ride with merchants and pilgrims, safest in a crowd. It takes longer, and you sleep every night.

events.text: You come out with nothing of the immortal's except dust in your hair and his letters in your head. At the gate the merchants glance at your empty hands and look past you to the next face. They are wrong about you, you think, and do not mind.

choices.text: Write down what you remember of the walls

effects.log: That night you fill twelve pages. It is not the legacy. It is not nothing either.

choices.text: Sell a story to the merchants instead

effects.log: They pay for a good account of the inside. You give them one, mostly true.

events.text: You slip out of the gate through a shadow on the mountain's side while the crowd watches the main mouth. Nobody sees you come out. For a whole evening, as far as the world knows, you are still in there, and you find you like the feeling of being nowhere.

choices.text: Enjoy the evening of being nobody

effects.log: You sit by a stream and eat a plain meal and are, for once, nobody's anything. It is wonderful.

choices.text: Go see who is waiting for you

effects.log: You come up behind the people waiting for you and watch them worry. Then you tap a shoulder. Their faces are worth the walk.

events.text: The masked fighters at the gate were waiting for whoever came out heavy, and they chose you. You cut through them, and in the scramble one mask comes loose: a face from your own road inside the cave, someone who smiled at you on the stair. They run, and you let them.

choices.text: Remember the face

effects.log: You will know them again. They know it. That will do more than chasing would.

choices.text: Call after them that you forgive them

effects.log: They stop, astonished, then run faster. Forgiveness frightens some people more than a blade.

events.text: Masked fighters wait in the rocks below the gate, the old way of men who could not win a realm and would rather rob someone who did. When it is over, one of them lies groaning with a bad ankle, his mask askew, younger than his voice. He came into the cave this morning too.

choices.text: Splint his ankle and send him home

effects.log: He stares at you the whole time you work. He will not ambush anyone again; you can see that much in his face.

choices.text: Leave him for his friends

effects.log: His friends do not come back for him. You do not either.

events.text: On the road out, something the immortal left in you wakes up: a line of the letters you never read, appearing behind your eyes as if it had always been there. It is not a technique. It is a way of standing when Heaven tells you to stand aside. You find you are standing that way already.

choices.text: Practise it in front of no one

effects.log: You stand that way in an empty field until it is as natural as breathing.

choices.text: Teach it to the first person who needs it

effects.log: A farmer arguing with a tax collector, a day later. You show them how to stand. The tax collector backs down, confused.

events.text: Past the barrier the valley opens into a field of hilts. Ten thousand swords stand in the glacier up to their guards, in rows that were straight four hundred years ago and have drifted with the ice, like grass leaning in a wind. When the wind does come, they hum, all of them, on one low note.

choices.text: Hum the note back

effects.log: Your voice is thin against ten thousand blades. But the nearest rows shift their pitch, just slightly, toward yours.

choices.text: Count the rows as you walk

effects.log: You give up at four hundred. Nobody has ever finished counting, they say, because the field does not want to be counted.

choices.text: Keep your own hand away from your weapon

effects.log: You walk with your hands open at your sides. The humming softens around you as you pass.

events.text: The cold of {sr_realm} is not the cold of winter. It goes for qi before it goes for skin, sliding into your meridians and slowing them, so that every breath of power has to be pushed like a cart through snow. The old entrants say: keep moving, keep warm, and never sleep among the swords.

choices.text: Circulate your qi hard to stay warm

effects.log: You burn hot and steady. It costs you, but your fingers keep their feeling all day.

choices.text: Let the cold in and learn its rhythm

effects.log: It hurts for an hour, then not. The cold has a pulse, very slow, and you can match it.

choices.text: Trade for a fur cloak at the barrier

effects.log: A merchant who will not go in sells you a cloak for far too much. It is worth it by noon.

events.text: {sr_sect}'s party goes in roped together, the old way, so that nobody wanders off into the field and nobody is left behind. On the rope in front of you is a young disciple who has never seen ice before, and who keeps reaching out toward the hilts as you pass, as if they were flowers.

choices.text: Tell them never to touch a hilt without asking

effects.log: "Asking who?" they say. "The sword," you say. They laugh, and then, seeing your face, stop reaching.

choices.text: Let them learn

effects.log: They touch one. The hilt is so cold it takes the skin of a fingertip, and the field's hum goes sharp for a moment. They do not reach again.

choices.text: Take the front of the rope yourself

effects.log: The leader lets you. You set the pace all morning, and the party comes through the first mile without a single slip.

events.text: You come in over the ridge, where there is no gate, only a place where the barrier sags like old cloth. Below, the sect parties file in through the proper gate with banners and ropes. Up here there is just you, the wind, and a sword someone else left in the snow on the ridge, as if they had climbed this far and changed their mind.

choices.text: Take the abandoned sword along

effects.log: It is a plain blade with a frozen tassel. In the field, as you pass, some of the swords seem to lean toward it.

choices.text: Plant it in the snow, point down, as a marker

effects.log: You leave it standing on the ridge. Whoever comes over next will know someone made it before them.

choices.text: Go down fast before anyone looks up

effects.log: You are among the hilts before the first sect banner reaches them. Nobody saw you come.

events.text: The note of the field changes as you walk in. Not much: a quarter tone, a breath. Old entrants stop and look around, frowning. You know why, and they do not. The swords recognised you. A past life walked between them, and they have kept its step the way ice keeps a footprint.

choices.text: Walk the old path again, deliberately

effects.log: You step where you stepped before. The hum rises behind you like a crowd remembering a name.

choices.text: Ask them, quietly, what you were like

effects.log: The answer comes as a ripple through the hilts, impossible to read and somehow not unkind.

events.text: In the third row of the field, a sword stands that is not like the others: newer steel, a different guard, a hilt wrapped in cord you know the knot of, because your hands still tie it that way. A past you came here and did not leave, and the field took the blade into its ranks, as if you had always been one of them.

choices.text: Kneel at the old sword

effects.log: The ice around it is clear as glass. You can see the whole blade, perfect, kept. You are oddly proud of it.

choices.text: Try to draw it out

effects.log: It does not move. The field hums a warning, gently. Whatever you were, it belongs to them now.

choices.text: Retie the cord on its hilt

effects.log: The old knot was coming loose. You tie it fresh, the same way. A small, foolish, necessary thing.

events.text: The cold finds every year you have lived and sits down in it. Your breath smokes, your knees creak, and the young of every party glance at you as if wondering who will carry you out. You have outlived better swordsmen than any of them, and the swords, you think, can tell.

choices.text: Walk at your own pace and let them stare

effects.log: You go slowly and never stop. By noon you have passed three of the young ones, who stopped to rest and could not get warm again.

choices.text: Teach a shivering youngster the old breathing for cold

effects.log: Four breaths in, hold, six out. They try it, then stare at you. "My hands are warm," they say, as if you had done magic.

events.text: You walk into the field and the humming stops. All of it, for a heartbeat, ten thousand swords falling silent to look at someone who should not be here. Then it starts again, slightly louder, and you cannot shake the feeling that the swords are laughing.

choices.text: Laugh with them

effects.log: You laugh at yourself, out loud, alone in the field. The hum changes, warmer. Being small and honest is a kind of passport.

choices.text: Stand straighter and walk on

effects.log: You walk the way you would if you were twice as strong. The field quiets, curious. Pride is not nothing here.

events.text: You have walked through many realms, and this is the first that feels like a battlefield after the battle, when everything is still standing but the people. Ten thousand oaths, kept in the ice. You know better than most what it costs to keep a promise that long.

choices.text: Salute the field as you would an army

effects.log: You raise your weapon in the old salute. All down the near rows the hilts tilt, very slightly, in reply.

choices.text: Walk the edges, where the oldest swords stand

effects.log: The oldest swords are the quietest. One of them, as you pass, sheds a sliver of ice you could swear was a tear. It is worth a fortune.

events.text: Your party's disciples look to you before they look at the swords, which is what it means to be an elder in a place like this. One of them asks what everyone wants to ask: "If a sword chooses one of us, Elder, does it belong to the sect, or to the one it chose?"

choices.text: "To the one it chose. A sword is not a coin."

effects.log: The disciples glance at each other. They will remember you said this when the time comes, and so will the sect.

choices.text: "To the sect. Everything we win, we win together."

effects.log: Heads nod, relieved. It is the easy answer, and it keeps the party whole today.

choices.text: "Ask the sword."

effects.log: They laugh. Then, deep in the field, one of them actually does ask, and the hum answers, and the laughter stops.

events.text: At the edge of the field someone has built a small shrine out of stacked ice and one plain sword, and on it is a wooden plaque with a name burned into it: Bang Gu-tae. Under the name, newer: "Who came out of the ice and lived forty years more, thanks to a stranger." You were the stranger. You remember his laugh.

choices.text: Light a stick of incense at the shrine

effects.log: The smoke rises straight up in the still air. The field's hum goes soft for a moment, as if it, too, remembers him.

choices.text: Read the rest of the plaque

effects.log: His grandchildren carved it. They do not know your name. They wrote: "If you are reading this, thank you." You are, so you accept it.

events.text: He is still there. At the edge of the field, standing in the ice up to his chest, a man with frost in his beard and eyes that move. Bang Gu-tae. You left him here in another life, with a promise you did not keep. His eyes find you at once across the hilts, and they are not angry. They are only tired, and glad.

choices.text: Go to him first, before anything else

effects.log: You press both hands to the ice over his heart and pour in your qi until you shake. A crack runs down from his collar. This time you will not leave.

choices.text: Tell him you are sorry, and that you came back

effects.log: His lips move behind the ice. You cannot hear the words, but you know them. "Then get me out."

events.text: A girl in a coat too thin for the glacier is walking the rows alone, holding up a sword hilt with no blade, like a lantern. Do Ye-rin, seventeen, apprentice at a village forge. "My grandmother came here sixty years ago and broke her sword on the ice and ran," she says, teeth chattering. "She made me promise to bring the hilt back to the blade. She said it would not forgive her otherwise."

choices.text: Give her your cloak

effects.log: She tries to refuse. You put it on her anyway. The cold bites into you at once, and she stops shaking, and that is worth it.

choices.text: Let her walk with you

effects.log: She falls in beside you, the hilt held out ahead, turning it toward the rows like a dowsing rod. "It gets warmer when it is close," she says.

choices.text: Tell her to go back to the gate

effects.log: "No," she says, simply, the way only the young and the old can. When you look back a while later, she is still following, twenty paces behind.

events.text: The hilt in Ye-rin's hands grows warm near a hollow where the ice has cracked and frozen again, and there it is, a broken blade, a forearm long, sunk in clear ice like a fish in a pond. Her grandmother's mark is on the steel. Ye-rin fits the hilt against the break, and the two halves will not join. "It needs heat," she whispers. "A forge. Out here, there is only us."

choices.text: Pour your qi into the join

effects.log: You hold the halves together and push heat through your palms until your vision goes white. When you let go, the seam glows dull red, and holds.

choices.text: Help her cut the blade free first, carefully

ok.log: You chip the ice a flake at a time while she warms the steel in her hands. The blade comes out whole, and she fits it home herself, crying.

fail.log: The ice splits badly and cuts your hands, but the blade comes free. She mends it with her breath and your blood-warm palms. It holds.

choices.text: Tell her the forge can wait until the gate

effects.log: She wraps both halves in your spare cloth and tucks them inside her coat. "Then it comes with us," she says. "Unmended. Like she was."

events.text: When it is over and the field lies still again, Ye-rin walks out into the middle of the risen swords with her grandmother's blade held out flat on both palms, the way a smith offers work to a master. Last Winter, at the head of the field, turns slowly on its point toward her. Then every sword in the valley dips, one row after another, like wheat.

choices.text: Kneel beside her

effects.log: You kneel in the snow next to her as the field bows. "She is forgiven," Ye-rin says, in a small astonished voice. "Isn't she?" You think so.

choices.text: Stand back and let the moment be hers

effects.log: You watch from the edge. It is not your story, and you are glad to have seen it.

events.text: You are down in the snow with the field of swords risen over you, points lowered, when Ye-rin steps between you and the nearest of them with her grandmother's blade in both hands, shaking so hard it rattles. "No," she says. And the swords stop. A smith's child, holding a sword a smith made, asking them to stop. They have not been asked for anything in four hundred years.

choices.text: Get up slowly behind her

effects.log: You rise. The swords sink back into the ice row by row, until the field is only hilts again. Ye-rin sits down very suddenly in the snow.

choices.text: Tell her she was very brave and very foolish

effects.log: "Grandmother said the same thing about herself," she says, and laughs, and does not stop shaking for an hour.

events.text: At the gate Ye-rin turns her grandmother's sword over in her hands in the ordinary daylight. It looks smaller out here. "I will forge one," she says suddenly. "Mine. Someday, when I am good enough. And I will make one for you, if you will let me. I do not know yet what it should be."

choices.text: Tell her to make it however she likes

effects.log: "Then it will take ten years," she says, very seriously. You will hear from a village forge, one day, that a blade is waiting with your name on its tang.

choices.text: Ask her to make it for someone who needs it more

effects.log: She looks at you for a long moment. "Grandmother would have liked you," she says, and bows like a disciple.

choices.text: Give her silver to set up her own forge

effects.log: She stares at the pouch. Then she takes it, because she is a smith and not a fool, and her bow nearly touches the snow.

events.text: At the edge of the field, a man is standing in the ice up to his chest, with frost in his beard and a hand still reaching for a sword that is not there. You think he is dead until his eyes move. They follow you. Old entrants say his name is Bang Gu-tae, that he tried to draw Last Winter at the last opening, and that the field has kept him alive ever since, as a warning.

choices.text: Press your hands to the ice and thaw him

effects.log: You pour qi into the ice until your arms shake. A crack runs from his collar to the ground, then another. He falls out into your arms, light as straw, and says, "What year is it?"

choices.text: Promise him you will free him on the way out

effects.log: His eyes close and open: yes. You mark the place in your memory, and go on into the field with his gaze on your back.

choices.text: Leave him; the field has its reasons

effects.log: You walk past. His eyes follow you as far as they can turn.

events.text: Bang Gu-tae walks beside you stiffly, like a man made of old wood, and asks questions nobody has been able to answer him in sixty years. Who rules now. What became of his sect. Whether rice still costs three coppers. And at last, carefully: "My wife. Seo-yun. She would be very old now. Do you think she waited?"

choices.text: Tell him the truth: you do not know

effects.log: "No," he agrees. "Nobody does." He walks a while. "I would not have wanted her to wait. I hope she did a little."

choices.text: Tell him she surely waited

effects.log: He smiles, and the smile cracks the last frost out of his beard. You do not know if it was a kindness or a cruelty. It felt like the first.

choices.text: Tell him rice is nine coppers now

effects.log: He stops dead in the snow. "Nine?" He is still muttering about it a mile later, and it seems to do him more good than anything.

events.text: All along the road the cold gets into your bones, and with it a thought you cannot shake: how long sixty years is when you spend them awake. Somewhere at your back, a man in the ice is counting the time until you come back. You catch yourself listening for him, and hearing only the hum of the swords.

choices.text: Tie a knot in your sleeve so you will not forget

effects.log: A silly thing. You touch it a dozen times before the guardian.

choices.text: Tell yourself you will decide at the gate

effects.log: It is a sensible plan. You notice you are not proud of it.

events.text: With the field quiet again and Last Winter hanging still in the air, Bang Gu-tae limps past you toward the sword that froze him, and stops an arm's length short. "I wanted it so badly," he says. "I do not even remember why." He looks at you. "Do not take it for the reason I would have. Whatever you take."

choices.text: Ask him what his reason was

effects.log: "To be the one who did," he says. "That was all. Sixty years for that." He laughs, an awful creaking laugh, and it sounds like freedom.

choices.text: Offer him whatever you carry out

effects.log: He steps back as if you had offered him a snake. "No. Never again." Then, softer: "But thank you. Nobody ever offered."

events.text: You are down, and the swords are coming, and Bang Gu-tae steps in front of you with his empty hands spread. The field knows him. It stops. "Take me back," he tells it, very calmly. "I was the greedy one. Not this one." Frost runs up his legs. He looks back at you over his shoulder. "Go on. You thawed me once. Somebody will again."

choices.text: Drag him back out of the frost

effects.log: You haul him by the collar out of the creeping ice, both of you shouting at each other. The field, astonished, lets you both go.

choices.text: Let him make his choice

effects.log: The ice closes over his chest, his shoulders. His eyes stay open, calm. You crawl away with his face behind you, and carry it the rest of your life.

events.text: Bang Gu-tae comes out of the gate into the world sixty years after he left it, blinking at the sun like a newborn. Half the crowd has heard of him. An old, old woman at the back of the crowd drops her walking stick, and he sees her, and the two of them stand very still.

choices.text: Step back and leave them to it

effects.log: You slip away while they are still staring at each other. Some stories should end without a witness. You will hear later that rice cost nine coppers at their wedding feast, the second one.

choices.text: Go over and introduce yourself

effects.log: Seo-yun takes your hand in both of hers and does not let go for a long time. She waited, a little. Then a lot.

events.text: On the way out you pass the place at the edge of the field. He is there, as you left him, eyes open, and they find yours. The gate is closing. Thawing him will cost you everything you have left, and you may not make the barrier before it seals.

choices.text: Keep the promise

effects.log: You press your palms to the ice and empty yourself into it. He falls out on the snow, and you drag each other through the gate with a breath to spare.

choices.text: Walk on, and tell yourself the next opening

effects.log: His eyes follow you to the gate. Sixty years. Someone else, you tell yourself. The ice keeps him, and the field keeps your face.

events.text: A tall swordswoman in crane-grey walks straight across the field to you and bows, exactly as deep as courtesy demands and not a hair deeper. "Cheon Ha-seong, of the Crane Ridge School. I am told you are the other one worth watching. The tomb will choose one of us. I would rather it chose honestly than that we cut each other to pieces first."

choices.text: Agree: let the field decide

effects.log: "Good." She smiles, briefly, the first crack in the frost of her manners. "Then we are not enemies until it has."

choices.text: Propose a duel now, to settle it

effects.log: Her eyes light. "After," she says. "If we both live. I want to see how you fight the swords first."

choices.text: Say a sword chooses its own hand, not a contest

effects.log: She considers this seriously. "Then I hope it chooses well," she says, and means it, which is rare.

events.text: Frost hounds come out of the snow on the far side of the field, a pack of them, pale as the drifts, and suddenly Ha-seong is at your back without a word, her blade out, guarding the side you cannot see. You fight the pack together, and it is strange how well it goes, like an old song two strangers both happen to know.

choices.text: Thank her when it is over

effects.log: "Do not," she says, wiping her blade. "I will need you whole when the field chooses. Nothing more." She is lying a little, and you both know it.

choices.text: Watch how she fights, and learn

effects.log: Her guard is beautiful and has one small gap, high on the left. You file it away, and are slightly ashamed of doing so.

events.text: With the field beaten back, Last Winter hangs in the air, and one sword rises from the ice and turns, slowly, between the two of you. Ha-seong stands very still. It hesitates over her, a long breath. Then it comes to your hand. Her face does not change at all, and you have never seen anyone hide something so completely.

choices.text: Offer to let her hold it once

effects.log: She looks at it, then at you. "No," she says. "It chose. That is the whole point." But she bows, deeper than at the start.

choices.text: Tell her the field hesitated over her

effects.log: "I saw," she says. "Next time it will not." It is not a threat. It is a promise, mostly to herself.

events.text: The field of swords has you down in the snow when Ha-seong walks in among them, blade sheathed, and hauls you out by the arm. The swords let her. She does not try for Last Winter herself. "Not like this," she says, breathing hard. "Not by stepping over you. The tomb would know."

choices.text: Tell her she could have had it

effects.log: "I know," she says. "That is why I could not." She sounds annoyed about it, which you like her better for.

choices.text: Promise you will repay her

effects.log: "In a duel," she says at once. "A real one, when you are whole." It is the most cheerful thing she has said all day.

events.text: Cheon Ha-seong finds you by the gate as the ice begins to thicken behind you. She does not mention the sword, or the field, or the hounds. "The Crane Ridge School holds a meet every spring," she says. "Come and lose to me there, when you have the time." She is gone into the crowd before you can answer.

choices.text: Go, next spring

effects.log: You will go. You will lose, the first time. The second time you will not, and she will laugh out loud, and you will have a rival for life.

choices.text: Shout after her that you will win

effects.log: Heads turn all across the gate. Somewhere in the crowd, she lifts one hand without turning round.

choices.text: Let it be a story for later

effects.log: Some meetings are better kept in the ice. You walk out of the valley with her name in your head and no plans to use it.

events.text: Snow crows follow every party through the field, big black birds with white-tipped wings that steal anything bright. One lands on a hilt beside you, cocks its head at the silver on your belt, and makes a noise exactly like a person clearing their throat.

choices.text: Bribe it with a coin

effects.log: It takes the coin, inspects it, and flies off. A minute later it drops something at your feet: an old jade ring, cold as the ice.

choices.text: Shoo it away

effects.log: It goes, offended. For the rest of the road there is always a crow somewhere behind you, watching, waiting for you to drop something.

events.text: The road between the rows narrows where the ice has pushed them close, and you must walk sideways between blades that stand at the height of your heart. Every hilt you pass is a person who chose this. You catch yourself reading the names scratched on the guards: Ha, Yun, Bo-ram, Old Third Brother.

choices.text: Read every name you pass aloud

effects.log: It slows you down. It seems the least anyone could do. The hum around you goes quiet and attentive, like a crowd at a funeral.

choices.text: Keep your eyes forward and get through

effects.log: You come out of the narrows quickly, chilled to the soul, with a dozen names you did not mean to remember.

events.text: The safe road keeps to the edge of the field, where the ice is old and solid and the swords are few. Every sect party seems to have chosen it, and the path is churned to slush by hundreds of boots. Ahead, a party from a lesser hall has stopped around one of their own, who has gone through a crust of rotten ice up to the thigh.

choices.text: Help them pull their disciple out

effects.log: It takes four of you and a rope. The young one comes out blue and swearing. Their elder grips your arm and does not say anything.

choices.text: Go round them and keep your place

effects.log: You lose nothing and gain nothing. The safe road is safe because it asks nothing of you.

events.text: The beast road runs through the high drifts where the frost hounds den. They hunt in silence, white against white, and you hear the first only when its breath steams beside your ear. Then there are six of them, circling, patient, waiting for the cold to slow you down.

choices.text: Fight back to back with a frozen hilt behind you

effects.log: You put your shoulders to a sword in the ice and fight. Each time a hound lunges, the old blade at your back hums like a warning, and you are ready.

choices.text: Throw them your rations and back away

effects.log: They fall on the food. You leave hungry, and in one piece.

choices.text: Stare down the pack leader

ok.log: The big hound meets your eyes for a long moment, then sits. The others follow. They watch you pass like a pack watching another pack.

fail.log: The leader is not impressed. You get out with torn sleeves and a new respect for silence.

events.text: Behind the hounds' drift there is a cave in the glacier, blue as the inside of a jewel, where the pack drags what it kills. Among the old bones are the things people carried in: packs, flasks, and one sword with no sheath, laid down carefully, as if by someone who knew they would not need it again.

choices.text: Take the silver from the packs

effects.log: Whoever carried it does not need it now. You take it and feel no better for it.

choices.text: Take only the sword, and bury it in the field

effects.log: You walk it back out and plant it in an empty place in the rows. The field hums as if it had been short one voice.

events.text: Your feet find a path no one else in the field can see: a tunnel in the glacier, opening behind a hilt you recognise by the chip in its guard. You knew it would be there. A past you cut this tunnel, by hand, a long time ago, and the ice has kept it open all these years like a door left on the latch.

choices.text: Go through alone

effects.log: The tunnel is blue and silent and warm, out of the wind. You come out halfway to the head of the field.

choices.text: Mark the entrance for someone in need

effects.log: You leave a small sign at the hilt. Someone will find it, cold and lost, and wonder who.

events.text: Halfway down the hidden tunnel there is a shelf cut into the ice, and on it a little bundle wrapped in oiled cloth and tied with a knot only your hands would tie. You undo it and laugh: a whetstone, a flask of ginseng tonic, a page of notes on the field, and a short message in your old hand. "You took long enough."

choices.text: Drink to the one who left it

effects.log: The tonic is very old and very good, bitter and warm all the way down. You drink to yourself, which is a strange and happy thing to do in a tomb.

choices.text: Study the notes

effects.log: Your past self watched the field carefully. Here is where Last Winter is weakest. Here is where it lies.

events.text: The road passes the place where a past life of yours fell. There is nothing there now but smooth ice and a single hilt standing a little apart from the others. The swords seem to have left a space around it, the way people leave room around a grave.

choices.text: Stand in the space a moment

effects.log: It is very quiet. You feel oddly safe there, as if the field were standing guard over you this time.

choices.text: Speak your old name to the ice

effects.log: The hilt rings, once, like a bell struck by a fingertip. The field answers on the same note.

events.text: When it is over the swords sink back into the ice, row after row, with a sound like a long breath let out. The field is only hilts again, humming their one low note. Far off at its head, Last Winter stands where it always stands, as if nothing has happened, as if nothing ever will.

choices.text: Sit in the snow until your hands stop shaking

effects.log: It takes a long time. The swords seem to wait with you.

choices.text: Bow to Last Winter before you go

effects.log: You bow to a sword. It is the most natural thing in the world, here.

events.text: Long after the fight, you can still hear it, the sound of ten thousand blades moving together, ringing in your ears and in the bones of your arms. Other entrants pass you on the snow and stare. You must look like someone who has been through a storm made of steel.

choices.text: Tell them what it was like

effects.log: You try. The words come out wrong and small. They nod anyway, pale, and you watch three of them turn back.

choices.text: Let the ringing teach you something

effects.log: In the ringing there is a rhythm, a beat the whole field moves to. You catch it, and keep it.

events.text: The field rises. Ten thousand swords come up out of the ice and fight you as one army, and Last Winter leads them with no hand on its hilt. You do not beat them. You beat the one at the front, and when Last Winter falls flat in the snow, every sword in the valley goes still and drops point-down, back into its oath. One stays in the air, turning slowly toward you.

choices.text: Hold out your hand to it

effects.log: It settles into your palm as if it had been waiting four hundred years for exactly this weight. Maybe it had.

choices.text: Ask its name before you take it

effects.log: The hilt is carved with a single word, worn almost flat. You speak it, and the blade warms in your hand.

events.text: As Last Winter goes down in the snow, you catch a glimpse of something that the old stories mention only in whispers: a woman in grey, standing among the risen swords, watching you with her arms folded. Mun Han-bi, the last master of Pale Ridge, four hundred years dead. She gives you one short nod, like an examiner. Then she is gone.

choices.text: Bow to the place she stood

effects.log: The snow there is undisturbed. You bow anyway, and feel the field approve.

choices.text: Call out to ask what she wanted of you

effects.log: The wind carries one word back across the field: "Remember." You will.

events.text: The field rises and you fight it, and for a few heartbeats you hold. Then there are simply too many. They do not cut to kill. They drive you down into the snow with the flats of ten thousand blades and stand over you in a ring, points lowered, waiting to see if you will rise. Their oath was never against people like you.

choices.text: Stay down; show them your open hands

effects.log: You lie still with your palms up. One by one the swords lift away and sink back into the ice. They did not want you. They wanted to be sure.

choices.text: Rise anyway

effects.log: You get up. The ring of swords watches you do it, and hums, and lets you walk out of it. Stubbornness, too, is a thing they understand.

events.text: You come round face down in the snow, colder than you have ever been, with a sword standing in the ice a finger's width from your cheek. It did not miss. It was put there, carefully, to show you what it could have done. Your breath has frozen to the steel.

choices.text: Thank it, and mean it

effects.log: The blade sinks back into the ice. You lie there a while longer, alive, learning what that word means.

choices.text: Get your qi moving before the cold wins

effects.log: You force the heat back through your meridians until you can stand. The effort leaves you hollow and stronger.

events.text: To pass the field without waking it, you have to walk among ten thousand blades without once meaning to draw your own. It is the hardest thing you have ever done. Halfway across, one sword stirs in the ice beside your knee, and you think of nothing, nothing at all, until it settles.

choices.text: Keep the empty mind as you walk on

effects.log: You walk out the far side of the field still holding it. You will be able to find it again.

choices.text: Breathe out at last, and laugh

effects.log: The laugh rings off the ice. Somewhere behind you, the field hums back, amused. It let you go.

events.text: You try to walk through the field with an empty heart, and it hears the one thing you could not empty: you want a sword. A row of blades jerks up out of the ice and turns you round, firmly, the way an adult turns round a child who has gone the wrong way, and you are sent sprawling back toward the start.

choices.text: Admit it: you wanted one

effects.log: Saying it aloud loosens something. The field hums, softer. Honesty, it seems, is a kind of key.

choices.text: Pick yourself up and walk the long way round

effects.log: It takes hours. You are frozen through when you reach the far side. You are also through.

events.text: Last time, in another life, the field put you down and you did not get up. You remember it as the swords rise: the cold, the ring of blades. This time Last Winter goes down in the snow before you do, and the field, very slowly, dips its points to you, the whole valley, like a crowd taking off its hats.

choices.text: Return the salute

effects.log: You raise your weapon. Ten thousand blades hum back. Whatever you lost here before, you have found it again.

choices.text: Go to the hilt that was yours

effects.log: You find it standing apart, and lay your hand on it. It is warm, for the first time.

events.text: You should not have won. The swords know it; you can hear it in the way the hum goes ragged all across the field, puzzled. Last Winter lies in the snow, beaten by someone it did not bother to take seriously. And then, quite clearly, from somewhere under the ice, comes a sound like a very old woman laughing.

choices.text: Laugh with her

effects.log: You laugh till you cry, alone in the frozen field. When you stop, a sword is waiting by your hand.

choices.text: Bow to the field for underestimating you

effects.log: It is a cheek, and the field takes it as one. The hum warms anyway.

events.text: The ice closes behind you with a sound like a door the size of a mountain. For a moment you can still hear the field humming through the barrier, ten thousand swords on one low note. Then the snow muffles it, and the valley is only a valley, white and quiet, keeping its oath for sixty more years.

choices.text: Listen until you cannot hear it

effects.log: You stand in the snow until the last of the note is gone. Your ears ring with the silence afterward.

choices.text: Hum the note to yourself on the road home

effects.log: For days you catch yourself humming it. Strangers look at you oddly. A blacksmith in one village stops working to listen.

events.text: Outside the gate the air is suddenly, absurdly warm. Your fingers burn as feeling comes back into them, and the crowd waiting at the gate is steaming like a pot. Someone hands you a cup of hot broth without asking who you are. It is the best thing you have ever tasted.

choices.text: Pay them double

effects.log: They wave the coin away. "You came out," they say. "That is payment enough." You leave it on their table anyway.

choices.text: Sit by their fire until you can feel your feet
