effects.log: You sit for an hour, listening to the others tell their stories. Most of them are lies. All of them are good.

events.text: At the gate you hand {sr_treasure} to {sr_sect}, as the party agreed. The elders take it carefully, and it is clear at once that it does not like being taken: the blade goes dull and cold in their hands. It stays bright only in yours. There is a long, uncomfortable silence.

choices.text: Insist they keep it, as agreed

effects.log: You leave it with them. It sulks in the sect's armoury for years, and every disciple who walks past it feels watched. The elders do not forget your word.

choices.text: Ask them to let it hang in the hall where you train

effects.log: A compromise. The elders agree, uneasily. The sword brightens whenever you walk in.

events.text: You carry out {sr_treasure} on your own back. It is heavier than steel should be, and it hums faintly against your spine all the way down the valley, as if still talking to the field. At the gate, every swordsman in the crowd looks at it, then at you, and does a sum.

choices.text: Let them do their sums

effects.log: You walk through the crowd with the sword on your back. Nobody tries. Not today.

choices.text: Wrap it in old cloth so it looks like nothing

effects.log: It does not like being hidden. But it keeps quiet, and so do you.

events.text: You walk out of the gate with no sword but the one you came in with, and somehow it feels different in your hand. Steadier. You wonder if it heard the field, all day long, and learned something from ten thousand older blades.

choices.text: Practise with it that night

effects.log: In the firelight your blade moves differently, more patient. Something rubbed off on it in there.

choices.text: Give it a name, at last

effects.log: You have carried it for years without one. You name it after the valley. It seems pleased.

events.text: You slip out the way you came over the ridge, while the crowd at the gate watches for the sect banners. From up here you can see the whole field below, ten thousand hilts in the sunset, and you are the only one who gets to see it like this, alone and on the way home.

choices.text: Sit on the ridge and watch until dark

effects.log: The hilts catch the last light one row at a time, like lamps being put out. You will remember it at the end of your life.

choices.text: Go down the far side quickly

effects.log: Nobody knows you came out. By the time they start asking, you are a day's walk away.

events.text: The ambush at the gate is better planned than most: three on the path, two on the ice above, all masked in white. You cut through them anyway, and as the last one falls, the sword you carry out sings, a single high note you have never heard steel make. The field, behind the closing barrier, answers it.

choices.text: Let the masks run

effects.log: They run. They will tell everyone about the singing sword, and nobody will try this again.

choices.text: Take a mask as a keepsake

effects.log: You will hang it in your room, white and blank. It reminds you how close it was.

events.text: Masked fighters in white come off the ice at the gate, fast and well drilled. When it is over and they have scattered, one mask lies in the snow, and under it, stitched into the lining, is a crest you know: a respectable hall, one whose elders stood smiling at the gate this morning.

choices.text: Keep the mask, and keep quiet

effects.log: You will have use for it someday, in a room full of smiling elders.

choices.text: Hold it up for the whole crowd to see

effects.log: There is a long silence, then a roar. That hall will not show its face at the next opening.

events.text: On the road out, the sword that chose you will not stay quiet. It tugs your hand toward every injustice you pass: a merchant cheating a farmer, a bully on a bridge. It seems it remembers its oath, and means to keep it in your hand too. No sword of Pale Ridge cuts for a tyrant. Some of them cut tyrants.

choices.text: Go where it pulls

effects.log: You spend a week on the road being tugged into other people's trouble. By the end, three villages know your face.

choices.text: Tell it firmly: you choose the fights

effects.log: It goes quiet, sulking. But the next time you draw it in anger, it is heavier, and you notice.

events.text: Past the barrier there is no ground, only glass: a silver lake running flat to every horizon under a white, sunless sky. You walk on your own reflection. It looks up at you from beneath your feet, matching you step for step, and the first thing you notice is that it looks more tired than you feel.

choices.text: Stop and look at it properly

effects.log: You look for a long time. It looks back. Neither of you says anything, and you come away knowing something you did not want to know about how you sleep.

choices.text: Look up and keep walking

effects.log: You keep your eyes on the white sky. Not looking at yourself turns out to be the hardest walk you have ever taken.

choices.text: Smile at it

effects.log: It smiles back a moment late, a little surprised. Your shoulders drop an inch you did not know they were holding.

events.text: The shards stand up out of the glass like broken sails, taller than houses, and every one shows something different. In one, a crowd at a gate. In one, an empty room. In one, a hand you know closing round a cup you have never seen. The old entrants say: do not stare into a shard unless you are ready to believe it.

choices.text: Walk between them with your eyes down

effects.log: You pass a hundred truths without looking. One of them calls your name, softly, in a voice you almost know.

choices.text: Look into the smallest one

effects.log: It shows you, a year from now, laughing at something. Only that. You carry it in for the rest of the day like a coin in your pocket.

choices.text: Touch one to see if it is cold

effects.log: It is warm, like skin. You take your hand away quickly, and the truth inside it shivers.

events.text: {sr_sect}'s party comes into the Mirror Realm in a tight knot, and for the first hour nobody can look at anybody else. The glass under each of them shows something a little different from the face they show the sect. By the second hour the party has quietly come apart into people walking alone.

choices.text: Gather them back together

effects.log: You make them walk shoulder to shoulder, eyes front, talking about nothing. It works, mostly. Two of them thank you at the gate.

choices.text: Let them walk alone; it is that kind of place

effects.log: You walk alone too. By the time you meet the others again, you all know each other a little better, and say nothing about it.

events.text: You slip in through a crack at the edge of the barrier, and the crack is in the mirror too: your reflection comes through it a heartbeat after you, squeezing, and for that heartbeat you are two people in two places. It is the strangest feeling in the world, and you are not sure which of you came out first.

choices.text: Decide it was you

effects.log: You decide. Your reflection, beneath your feet, does not argue. Not yet.

choices.text: Wait for your reflection to settle

effects.log: It catches up, step by step, until it matches you again. Nobody saw either of you come in.

events.text: Your reflection in the glass is not quite your face. It is the face you wore when a past life walked this lake, older or younger, a little different around the eyes. It looks up at you with recognition, as if it has been waiting here the whole time for you to come back and take its place.

choices.text: Kneel and lay your palm on the glass over it

effects.log: Its palm meets yours from below. For a moment you know exactly what that life wanted, and whether it got it.

choices.text: Tell it you are someone else now

effects.log: It nods, slowly, and as you walk on, its face settles into yours. It was only waiting to hear it.

events.text: Somewhere in this lake a past life of yours died, and the realm remembers. Your reflection walks beneath you with its eyes closed, the way people walk past a place they cannot bear to look at. Then, as you reach the first shards, it opens them, and looks up at you with an expression you have only ever seen on mourners.

choices.text: Ask it how you died

effects.log: It shakes its head. Some truths, even here, are not for the asking. It walks on beside you, closer than before.

choices.text: Promise it you will walk out this time

effects.log: It looks at you a long time. Then, slowly, it nods, as if you had made the promise for both of you.

events.text: Your reflection is younger than you. Not much: ten years, perhaps fifteen. It walks beneath you with a spring you lost long ago, and looks up at you with a frank, unkind curiosity, as if wondering how it is going to end up like this.

choices.text: Tell it: "Better than you think."

effects.log: It frowns, then laughs. By the shards its face has aged to match yours, and it seems content.

choices.text: Say nothing, and outwalk it

effects.log: You keep a steady pace. It tires before you do. Age, it turns out, is a kind of stamina.

events.text: Your reflection in this realm is stronger than you. You can see it at once: the set of its shoulders, the qi moving under its skin like light under water. It looks up at you with an odd, gentle pity, the way the strong sometimes look at the person they used to be.

choices.text: Ask it how it got so strong

effects.log: "I stopped lying to you," it says, and walks on, and will say no more.

choices.text: Refuse to look at it

effects.log: You walk with your head up and your eyes on the sky. Your neck aches by noon. You do not look down.

events.text: You have seen the inside of many realms. This one turns the habit around: it is the only realm that comes into you. Every veteran's trick is useless here. There is no map of a lake that shows you yourself, and every entrant walks it alone, however many friends they came with.

choices.text: Walk it as a beginner

effects.log: You let go of everything you know about realms. It is uncomfortable and the lake rewards it.

choices.text: Trust your instincts anyway

effects.log: Some of what you know works even here. You find a shard nobody else noticed, with a pouch of silver frozen in it.

events.text: Your disciples will not look down. You can see them trying not to, all across the glass, walking with their chins up and their eyes watering. One of them finally asks, very quietly, what you see when you look at your own reflection here, Elder. The others all lean in to hear.

choices.text: Tell them the truth

effects.log: You tell them. It is not flattering. There is a long silence, and then, one by one, they start looking down, braver for it.

choices.text: "An elder. What else?"

effects.log: They laugh, relieved. It is not the truth, and you all know it, and it gets them through the first mile.

events.text: Your reflection in the glass is wearing your face and smiling a smile you have never smiled. The heart demon is in there with it. Down here it does not have to whisper. It walks beneath you in plain sight, and every few steps it looks up and mouths a word you would rather not read.

choices.text: Stop and stare it down

effects.log: You stare at it until your eyes ache. It looks away first. For now, that will do.

choices.text: Read the word it is mouthing

effects.log: You read it. It is your own name, said the way you say it to yourself on bad nights. Something in your chest goes hot and ugly.

choices.text: Walk on and refuse to look down

effects.log: You walk with your eyes on the white sky all the way to the shards. Behind you, beneath you, it laughs.

events.text: Your reflection is not one person. As you walk it changes: a face, then another, then another, all of them yours, every life the soul has lived passing beneath your feet like fish under ice. Then it settles on the face you wear now, and looks up at you as if to ask which of them you think you are.

choices.text: Answer: "All of them."

effects.log: The reflection nods slowly. For a moment the faces flicker together, and you feel very old and very steady.

choices.text: Answer: "Only this one."

effects.log: It nods too, differently. The other faces fade. The life you are in feels, for a while, like enough.

events.text: Before you have taken ten steps on the glass, your reflection waves. First. Before your hand moves. In another life you let it walk out beside you, and it seems it has been waiting here since, not beneath you but beside you, ready to walk out again. It falls in at your side on the silver like an old friend.

choices.text: Walk with it, shoulder to shoulder

effects.log: You cross the lake two abreast, you and yourself. Nobody else in the realm has ever looked so unafraid.

choices.text: Ask it what it did, after it came out

effects.log: "Watched you," it says. "Every life. You do the same things wrong. It is very dear."

events.text: There is a small figure made of glass sitting on the silver at the barrier, with a thread of red cord around one wrist, the cord you tied there in another life. The Glass Child. "You said you would come back," she says, not reproachful, only pleased to be right. "I have been practising which one is real. Ask me."

choices.text: Ask her

effects.log: "You," she says at once, pointing at you, and then at your reflection: "And also you." She claps. She has worked it out.

choices.text: Untie the cord and tie it on yourself

effects.log: She holds out her wrist solemnly. It was a promise; now it is yours to keep again.

events.text: A child made of glass is sitting on the silver, clear as water, with no reflection under her at all. She watches you come with great interest. "You have two," she says, pointing at you and then at the glass beneath your feet. "Which one is real? I ask everybody. Nobody knows."

choices.text: "Me, of course."

effects.log: "That is what everybody says," she tells you kindly, and gets up to follow you. "But the one under you says it too."

choices.text: "Both of us."

effects.log: Her eyes go wide. "Nobody says that." She takes your hand. Her fingers are cool and smooth as a cup.

choices.text: "I do not know. Do you?"

effects.log: "No," she says, delighted. "That is why I ask." She falls in beside you as if you were old friends.

events.text: The Glass Child chatters as you walk. She is the reflection of Ok Ga-eun, the mirror-maker's daughter, she explains, left in the glass when the real Ga-eun was eight. "She grew up and walked out, and I stayed eight. Everyone says she was very old when she died. I would like to see her. Do you think I could?"

choices.text: Promise to take her out with you

effects.log: She squeezes your hand so hard it hurts. "Promise properly." You tie a red thread round her glass wrist. She stares at it as if it were gold.

choices.text: Tell her the truth: Ga-eun is long gone

effects.log: She is quiet for a long time. "I know," she says at last. "I wanted someone to say it." She keeps hold of your hand.

events.text: When it is over, the Glass Child walks out onto the glass where your reflection waits and crouches over it, and looks from it to you and back with a frown of tremendous concentration. "Oh," she says. "Now I see. The real one is the one who keeps walking." She pats your reflection on the head, kindly, like a puppy.

choices.text: Ask her if that is the answer, then

effects.log: "It is my answer," she says firmly, which is the best kind. Your reflection, beneath you again, seems to agree.

choices.text: Thank her for being kind to it

effects.log: "Somebody should," she says. "You are very hard on it." You are. You feel oddly ashamed.

events.text: Your reflection has you down on the glass and is standing over you when the Glass Child walks between you and takes its hand, as calmly as taking a parent's hand in a market. It stops. It looks down at her, and its face, your face, goes soft in a way you have never seen it go in any mirror.

choices.text: Get up while it is distracted

effects.log: You get up. It lets you. It is still holding her hand when you step away, and it does not seem to mind.

choices.text: Stay down and watch your own face like that

effects.log: You lie on the glass and look at yourself being gentle. It is the most useful thing the realm shows you all day.

events.text: At the gate the Glass Child stops at the edge of the barrier and cannot go on. It is like a window to her. She presses both hands to it and looks out at the real world, at the grass and the crowd and an ordinary blue sky, which she has never seen. "It is very bright," she says. "Is it always?"

choices.text: Carry her out inside a shard

effects.log: You hold up a shard of glass, and she steps into it like a child climbing into a cart. It is warm in your hand all the way home. Sometimes, at night, it laughs.

choices.text: Promise to come back for her

effects.log: She nods, very seriously, and holds up her wrist with your red thread on it. "I will be practising," she says.

choices.text: Tell her yes, it is always this bright

effects.log: She stands at the barrier and looks for as long as you stay. When you finally go, she waves. You wave back until the gate closes.

events.text: At the barrier a fortune-teller in faded indigo is reading palms for coppers, and she reads yours without being asked. "A long road," she says. "They all say that." She lets go. "I am Jin Sa-wol. My husband drowned twenty years ago, and they never found him. They say the shards show the truth. I would like company while I look."

choices.text: Walk with her

effects.log: "Good," she says, gathering her cards. "I can tell fortunes, but not my own. It is a professional limitation."

choices.text: Pay her for the reading and go on alone

effects.log: She pockets the coin with a professional nod. "You will see me again," she says. "That one is free."

events.arc: The One Who Wanted the Truth

events.text: Sa-wol finds her shard by the way she stops breathing. In it, a man of sixty is laughing at a table in a town she does not know, with grey in his hair and a grandchild on his knee. He did not drown. He walked away from the river and kept walking. She kneels on the glass and looks at him for a long time.

choices.text: Kneel beside her and say nothing

effects.log: You stay with her until she is ready. When she stands, her face is calm, the way a field is calm after a storm has finished with it.

choices.text: Tell her what it means, plainly

effects.log: "He left," you say. "I know," she says. "I have known for twenty years. I wanted to be sure he was happy, so I could stop." She sounds almost grateful.

choices.text: Turn her away from it

effects.log: You put a hand on her shoulder and turn her toward the white sky. She lets you. "Thank you," she says. "That was enough of it."

events.arc: The One Who Wanted the Truth

events.text: Far across the lake you find the fortune-teller again, kneeling before a shard, perfectly still. In it a grey-haired man laughs at a table in some far town with a child on his knee. She does not look round as you come up. "He did not drown," she says. "He walked. I predicted it twenty years ago and did not believe myself."

choices.text: Sit with her a while

effects.log: You sit on the glass beside her. Neither of you says anything. After a time she gathers herself up as if gathering cards.

choices.text: Ask her what she will do now

effects.log: "Stop waiting," she says. "It is very strange. I do not know what to do with my hands."

events.arc: The One Who Wanted the Truth

events.text: Sa-wol walks out of the gate beside you, blinking in the plain daylight, and stops to shuffle her cards, out of habit. Then she lays one face up, looks at it, and gives a short surprised laugh. "Here is your fortune, free," she says. "The next door opens in {sr_years} years: {sr_next}. And this time, I believe me."

choices.text: Help her write a letter to the man in the shard

effects.log: She writes four lines. You do not read them. She gives it to a carter going east. "Not to make him come back," she says. "Just to make him know."

choices.text: Ask her to read your fortune properly

effects.log: She takes your hand and reads it for a long time, and tells you one thing you did not know about yourself. It is true.

choices.text: Walk her to the crossroads

effects.log: At the crossroads she chooses a road she has never taken. You watch her go until she is a speck. She does not look back.

events.arc: The One Who Wanted the Truth

events.text: A mile onto the lake you notice it. Your reflection is a step behind you. Then, when you stop, it takes one more step, and stands a pace ahead, looking back up at you through the glass with an expression that is very much its own. It has been waiting to be noticed. You have the feeling it has been waiting your whole life.

choices.text: Stop and wait for it to speak

effects.log: It does not speak. It only nods, once, the way you nod to someone you will talk to later.

choices.text: Stamp on the glass

effects.log: It flinches, and then, slowly, it smiles. It is not a nice smile. It is yours.

choices.text: Ask it what it wants

effects.log: "Later," it mouths. Its lips move a beat before yours would. "When you are tired."

events.text: When you are tired, it speaks. Its voice comes up through the glass, your voice, without the parts you put on for other people. It knows the thing you have never told anyone. It says it plainly, the way you never could. Then it offers a trade. "Let me out at the end, and I will carry it for you. You will never have to think about it again."

choices.text: Agree to the bargain

effects.log: "Good," it says, and for the rest of the road your step is lighter, and something in your chest is hot and empty where the old weight was.

choices.text: Refuse: it is yours to carry

effects.log: It looks up at you for a long time. "Then carry it," it says, "and I will watch you do it." It sounds, for a moment, proud.

choices.text: Ask why it wants out so badly

effects.log: "Because I have spent your whole life being looked at and never seen," it says. "Have you?" You have no answer. It accepts that as a refusal.

events.text: You beat your reflection, and it lies on the glass laughing, because it has won anyway. "The bargain," it reminds you. "At the gate, I walk out with your weight, and you walk out light." It holds up its hand for you to help it up. Its hand is warm. Yours, you notice, has gone cold.

choices.text: Help it up, and keep the bargain

effects.log: It rises beside you, not beneath you, and walks with you toward the gate as a second shadow. You feel wonderful. You feel nothing.

choices.text: Break the bargain now

effects.log: You take your hand back. Its face falls, then, strangely, relaxes, as if it too were glad. "You are harder than I thought," it says, and sinks back into the glass.

events.text: You beat your reflection, and it lies on the glass looking up at you with your own eyes. "You kept it," it says. "The weight. I offered to take it and you kept it." It does not sound angry. "Then let me walk out with you anyway. Not to carry it. Just to see."

choices.text: Let it walk beside you

effects.log: It rises, and walks with you, not beneath you but beside you, and the weight between you is easier shared.

choices.text: Tell it its place is below the glass

effects.log: It nods without argument and sinks back down. Every step to the gate, it matches you perfectly. You have never been so well accompanied.

events.text: You slip past the place where your reflection waits by thinking of anything but yourself, and it lets you, which is the strange part. When you are through it calls up after you through the glass, in your own voice: "You only got past because I wanted to see where you would go. So take me there."

choices.text: Hold out your hand to the glass

effects.log: Its hand comes up to meet yours, and then it is standing beside you on the silver, faint as breath, looking around with great interest.

choices.text: Tell it to watch from where it is

effects.log: "I always do," it says, and settles back into step beneath you, matched and patient.

events.text: Your reflection beats you, which should be impossible, since it only knows what you know. But it is not afraid of what you are afraid of. It kneels on your chest, light as glass, and looks down at your face, and for a moment you see how you look to it: like someone it has been trying to reach for years.

choices.text: Ask it what it was trying to say

effects.log: It tells you. It takes one sentence. You will not repeat it to anyone, ever, and you will think about it every day.

choices.text: Push it off and get up

effects.log: You throw it off. It lands lightly and watches you rise, and nods, satisfied. It wanted to see that too.

events.text: At the gate your reflection stands beside you in the daylight like a second person, faint as breath on a window. Nobody in the crowd seems to see it. It looks at the grass and the people and the blue sky with tremendous attention, as if trying to learn the whole world in the one moment before the gate closes.

choices.text: Walk out together

effects.log: You step out of the gate side by side. After that your shadow is always a little darker than other people's, and sometimes it is facing the wrong way.

choices.text: Send it back, gently, at the last moment

effects.log: You touch its shoulder, and it understands, and steps back into the glass of the gate. It waves as the gate closes. You will meet it again, it says, in some other mirror.

events.text: At the gate you look down into the last pane of silver and your reflection looks up at you. Matched again, step for step. It lifts its hand when you lift yours. Only at the very last moment, as the gate begins to close, does it do one thing on its own: it nods to you, once, the way equals do.

choices.text: Nod back

effects.log: You nod. It is gone. Afterward, in every mirror you pass, you catch yourself checking whether it nods first.

choices.text: Say goodbye aloud

effects.log: You say it. Nobody at the gate understands who you are talking to, and you do not explain.

events.text: Glass moths drift over the lake, the size of a palm, wings like thin mirrors, and wherever they settle on someone they show the people nearby one small true thing: a lie told that morning, a kindness nobody noticed. A whole party ahead of you is walking with their arms over their heads to keep them off.

choices.text: Let one settle on you

effects.log: It lands on your shoulder. The nearest stranger looks over, reads what it shows, and gives you a small, surprised bow.

choices.text: Wave them off and keep moving

effects.log: You keep them away all road long. Nobody learns anything about you today, and you are tired from the effort.

events.text: Halfway across the lake you pass another entrant going the other way, toward the barrier, weeping quietly. You stop. They look at you, and then down at your reflection, and then, for a long moment, at their own. "It is only true," they say. "That is all it ever is. Only true." And they walk on.

choices.text: Walk them back to the barrier

effects.log: It costs you an hour. At the barrier they thank you without looking up. You never learn what they saw.

choices.text: Let them go, and look at your own reflection

effects.log: You look. It looks back. It is only true. You walk on, a little more careful of yourself.

events.text: The safe road is marked by a line of old red cords tied around shards, left by other openings so that people could find their way without looking into anything. Following it, you can cross the lake with your eyes on the cords and never see a truth you did not ask for.

choices.text: Follow the cords exactly

effects.log: You reach the far side without a single look. It is a very calm walk. You feel, oddly, that you have missed something.

choices.text: Retie a cord that has come loose

effects.log: You tie it back to its shard, tight, for whoever follows. Your eyes slide across the shard as you work, and catch one small, kind truth.

events.text: The beast road runs where the lake shows things that never lived: the reflections of beasts with nothing to reflect, great shapes moving under the glass like fish under ice. Now and then one comes up, slides out of the silver, and stands on the lake, real enough to bite.

choices.text: Fight it as if it were real

effects.log: It is real enough. You come away scratched and shaking, and the beast sinks back into the glass in pieces of light.

choices.text: Tell it, firmly, that it never lived

effects.log: It hesitates. Then, slowly, it believes you, and goes flat and silver and still on the glass.

choices.text: Run, and do not look down

effects.log: You run for a mile with things moving under your feet. When you finally stop, nothing has followed you.

events.text: Where the beasts of the glass have fought, the lake is cracked into a field of fine shards, each the size of a fingernail. Each of them shows something true, very small. A jeweller would pay well for a pouch of them, if a jeweller could stand to look at them.

choices.text: Fill a pouch

effects.log: You fill it without looking at any of them. It is heavy and faintly warm, and it murmurs when you walk.

choices.text: Pick one, and look at it

effects.log: It shows you a choice you made years ago, from the outside. You were right. You did not know until now.

events.text: Your reflection turns off the road before you do. It stops beneath your feet and points: a way across the glass you cannot see but it can, because it walked here in a past life and remembers. You follow it, step for step, for once the one who matches.

choices.text: Follow it all the way

effects.log: It leads you through a gap in the shards to a stretch of lake that shows nothing at all but sky. It is very peaceful.

choices.text: Thank it at the end

effects.log: It looks surprised to be thanked. It has been doing this for you for a long time.

events.text: On the hidden road there is a single shard standing alone, and in it, very clearly, a face you wore in a past life, holding up a folded paper and smiling. When you touch the shard the paper is in your hand, warm, as if it had just been passed across a table. It is a letter to whoever you would be next.

choices.text: Read it

effects.log: It is short and practical, and it ends: "Do not be afraid of the reflection. It is only you, without the armour." You keep it.

choices.text: Write a reply on the back and put it back

effects.log: You write to the life before. You thank them. The shard takes the paper back, and the face in it, for a moment, reads.

events.text: One shard shows a person waiting at a doorway with a lamp: {echo_spouse}, who was married to {echo_name}, the life before this one. It is not a memory. It is the truth, now: they are old, and still look up at the door whenever the wind moves it, {echo_years} years later.

choices.text: Watch until they put the lamp out

effects.log: They put it out at last and go in. You stand before the dark shard a long time.

choices.text: Tap the glass, once, gently

effects.log: In the shard, {echo_spouse} looks up sharply at the door. Then they smile, for no reason they could name.

events.text: A shard on the road shows {echo_killer}, who ended the life of {echo_name}. Not then: now. They are sitting alone in a bare room, older, staring at their own hands. The mirror shows what it shows. It does not choose sides.

choices.text: Forgive them, aloud, here

effects.log: You say it to the shard. They cannot hear. You can. Something in your chest unclenches a finger's width.

choices.text: Look until you are satisfied

effects.log: You look a long time. You are not satisfied. The heat in your chest is old, and familiar, and grows.

choices.text: Walk past it

effects.log: It is not your life anymore. You walk on. The shard is behind you, and then it is gone.

events.text: A shard shows {echo_name}, the life before yours, at the age it ended: {echo_age}, so young, standing on this same lake in some other opening, looking up at you through the glass as if it knows you. It died of {echo_cause}. It looks at the years you have now with open envy.

choices.text: Show it your hands, older than it ever got

effects.log: It looks at your hands for a long time, and nods, satisfied. Someone got the years. That seems to be enough.

choices.text: Promise to use them well

effects.log: It holds you to it with one long look. You feel the promise settle into you like a stone into a riverbed.

events.text: When it is over your reflection is back beneath your feet, matching you exactly, as if nothing happened. It lifts its hand when you lift yours. Only its eyes are different: it looks at you now as if you had both learned something, and neither of you is going to say what.

choices.text: Look at it as long as it looks at you

effects.log: Neither of you looks away. When at last you walk on, you feel more yourself than you have in years.

choices.text: Walk on and leave it be

effects.log: You walk on. It walks with you, perfectly matched. That is its own kind of truce.

events.text: Afterward, you sit down on the glass because your legs will not hold you, and your reflection sits down beneath you at the same moment. Around you, other entrants are facing their own, here and there across the lake, in silence. Nobody can help anybody. It is the loneliest crowd you have ever been part of.

choices.text: Watch someone else's fight

effects.log: You watch a stranger stand still and let their reflection strike them. It stops. They hug it. You look away.

choices.text: Close your eyes and breathe

effects.log: You breathe until the shaking stops. When you open your eyes your reflection is breathing with you.

events.text: Your reflection fights with every move you know, and knows every weakness you hide. You beat it the only way possible: by doing something you have never done before. It falls back on the glass, astonished, and beyond it, standing up out of the silver like a tooth, is a shard of the mirror that shows the truth.

choices.text: Help your reflection up first

effects.log: It takes your hand from below the glass. For a moment you are holding your own hand, and it is warm.

choices.text: Remember what you did, so you can do it again

effects.log: You fix it in your mind. It was not a technique. It was a decision. It will not be the last.

events.text: Your reflection beats you with your own art, and your own habits, and every corner you have ever cut. It stands over you on the glass, breathing hard, wearing your face, and you have never seen your face look so disappointed. Then, slowly, it holds out its hand.

choices.text: Take its hand

effects.log: It pulls you up. Its grip is exactly as strong as yours, no more. You realise it could not have won without your help.

choices.text: Get up on your own

effects.log: You get up. It nods, as if that was the right answer too, and sinks back beneath the glass.

events.text: You cannot slip past your own reflection by hiding: it sees everything you see. You slip past it the only other way. You stop looking at yourself. One step, then another, eyes on the white sky, thinking of someone else entirely, until you are past the place where it waits and it is left looking up at nobody.

choices.text: Keep thinking of that someone

effects.log: You think of them all the way to the gate. It is the best road you have ever walked.

choices.text: Look back down once you are past

effects.log: It is looking up at you, amused, and a little hurt. You owe it a proper fight someday.

events.text: You try not to look at yourself, and of course you do. Your reflection is waiting the moment your eyes drop, and it steps up out of the glass and into your way, and stops you with one hand on your chest. "Not like that," it says. "Not by pretending I am not here."

choices.text: Admit it is there

effects.log: "You are here," you say. It nods, and takes its hand away, and that is the end of it.

choices.text: Push past it anyway

effects.log: It lets you push it, and you fall over your own feet. It is a very humbling lesson, delivered by yourself.

events.text: You remember now: a past life fought its reflection here, and lost, and did not come out. This time your reflection goes down, and lies on the glass, and looks up at you with relief. "You came back," it says. "I have been waiting to lose to you. Thank you."

choices.text: Tell it there was no need to wait

effects.log: "I did," it says. "That is what a reflection is for." It sinks back into the glass, smiling your smile.

choices.text: Ask what the last life lacked

effects.log: "Nothing," it says. "It just looked away at the wrong moment." You resolve not to.

events.text: Your reflection was stronger than you. It said so at the barrier. And you have beaten it, somehow, and it sits on the glass rubbing its jaw and staring at you with real respect. "I was stronger," it says. "You were braver. I did not know that was allowed."

choices.text: "Neither did I."

effects.log: It laughs, your laugh, and holds out its hand. You shake on it, an agreement neither of you understands yet.

choices.text: Ask it to teach you its strength

effects.log: "I already have," it says. "Look at your hands." You look. They are steadier than they were this morning.

events.text: When your reflection is beaten, it does not fight to rise. It looks past you instead, at the empty space beside you, the place where someone would stand if you had ever let anyone stand there. "You came into this life swearing you would not be alone again," it says. "Look how close you are to keeping it. Or not."

choices.text: Tell it you will not waste this life

effects.log: It nods, and the empty space beside you feels, for a moment, less empty. As if someone just stepped out for a minute.

choices.text: Tell it some people are meant to walk alone

effects.log: "Maybe," it says. "But you were not, last time. You said so. I heard you."

events.text: Your reflection has you down, and it does not strike. It kneels on the glass, and in the silver behind it, very faintly, there is a small figure holding its hand: a child who was never born. Your last life wished for one at the end, and the mirror kept the wish. "Not a reproach," your reflection says. "A reminder."

choices.text: Look at the child as long as it is there

effects.log: It fades slowly. You will not forget the shape of it. You are not sure if that is a mercy.

choices.text: Get up and say you understood

effects.log: You rise. Your reflection steps aside. The little figure in the silver waves before it goes.

events.text: You beat your reflection, and as it falls you see the face your last life died with: young, surprised, cut off. It looks up at you, at the years already in your face. "You got further," it says, a little jealous, mostly glad. "Get further still. Live to grey for me."

choices.text: Promise it

effects.log: You promise. It smiles, and grows older as you watch, until it wears your face again.

choices.text: Tell it you are only getting started

effects.log: It laughs, delighted. "Good. Then I will keep watching."

events.text: Your reflection beats you, easily, and stands over you shining with a realm you have not reached: the height your last life stood at, and you have not climbed back to. "You remember being this," it says. "So do I. Every day. Is it the height you miss, or the view?"

choices.text: "The view."

effects.log: It nods slowly and the glow fades from it. "Then climb for the view," it says. "Not to get back. To see."

choices.text: "The height."

effects.log: It shrugs, your shrug, and helps you up. "Then you will climb faster and enjoy it less. Your choice."

events.text: When you beat your reflection, it does not fall alone. In the glass behind it stands someone your last life failed: faint, patient, not angry. They died because of you, or without you, and you came into this life to make it right. Your reflection looks from them to you. "They are not here to blame you," it says. "They came to see if you are still trying."

choices.text: Tell them you are

effects.log: The figure in the glass bows its head, once, and fades. Your hands are shaking, and lighter.

choices.text: Ask them how

effects.log: The figure says nothing. It only points: outward, at the world. At everyone else you have not failed yet.

events.text: Your reflection fights you with your rival's moves. Every one of them: the feint, the low cut, the habit of the left foot, all the things you watched for a whole life and never beat. It puts you down with the move that beat you last time. "You still flinch from it," it says. "I know. I am the flinch."

choices.text: Make it do the move again

effects.log: It does. Again. And again. On the ninth time you stop flinching, and it smiles, and stands aside.

choices.text: Ask it what the rival feared

effects.log: It tells you. It is so simple that you laugh out loud on the glass. You knew it all along.

events.text: Your reflection goes down, and as it falls its art falls with it, move by move, pouring out onto the glass like water and draining away into the silver. All the art you carried in your last life, with no one to give it to. "It goes like that," your reflection says, "when nobody takes it. Will you let it go like that again?"

choices.text: Say no: you will teach this time

effects.log: The draining art stops, and pools, and you can see the shape of it, waiting to be handed on.

choices.text: Gather what you can with your hands

effects.log: You scoop at the silver. A little of it stays in your palms. Enough to teach one person, if you find the right one.

events.text: Your reflection is the heart demon. Here, nothing hides it. You fight it, your own face twisted into its smile, and you win, and it lies on the glass hissing. Beaten, it is smaller than you thought. It always was. It just stood very close.

choices.text: Hold it down until it is quiet

effects.log: You hold it down with one hand until it stops struggling and is only your reflection again, tired and ordinary.

choices.text: Let it go, and let it see you walk away

effects.log: It watches you walk away. It cannot follow, here. Not for a while.

events.text: The heart demon wears your reflection, and it wins. It sits on your chest on the glass, light as nothing, heavy as everything, and smiles your smile at you. "Every time you look in a mirror, from now on," it says, "you will see me first." It is not a threat. It is a description.

choices.text: Say: "Then I will look anyway."

effects.log: Its smile flickers, just slightly. It did not expect that. It gets off your chest without being asked.

choices.text: Close your eyes until it goes

effects.log: It goes, eventually. You do not open them for a long time after.

events.text: Your reflection fights you wearing a face from before: {echo_name}, who died of {echo_cause}. It fights the way that life fought, which is not the way you fight, and the strangeness of it is the whole battle. When it is over, it is your own face again, and it says: "Thank you for carrying me this far."

choices.text: Tell it you will carry it further

effects.log: It nods, and smiles a smile that belongs to two lives at once.

choices.text: Ask it what it would have done differently

effects.log: It thinks for a long time. "Nothing," it says. "But I would have been less afraid." You file that away.

events.text: Behind you the Mirror Realm closes like an eye. The barrier silvers over, and for one long moment it is a mirror the size of a mountain, showing the whole crowd at the gate to itself: every face, every expression, everything they are pretending not to feel. Then it fades to air, and people start talking very loudly.

choices.text: Look for your own face in it before it goes

effects.log: You find it, near the front. It looks like someone who has been through something, and is all right. You believe it.

choices.text: Watch the crowd see itself instead

effects.log: You watch a hundred people see themselves at once. It is better than any find. Some of them go home and change.

events.text: On the road home it rains, and every puddle you pass shows you your face. You keep checking, without meaning to, whether it moves when you move, whether it looks back. It does. Of course it does. And still you find yourself nodding to it now and then, like an acquaintance.

choices.text: Keep nodding

effects.log: You nod to every puddle on the road. A child sees you do it and starts nodding to puddles too.

choices.text: Stop looking at puddles

effects.log: It takes a week to break the habit. Your reflection, presumably, does not mind.

events.text: At the gate you hand {sr_treasure} to {sr_sect}, as the party agreed. The elder who takes it glances into it, out of curiosity, and goes grey. Nobody asks what the elder saw. The shard is wrapped in black silk and carried away, and for a long time after nobody in the hall will look at it.

choices.text: Ask the elder, privately, if they are all right

effects.log: They look at you for a long time. "No," they say. "But I will be. Thank you for asking." They mean it.

choices.text: Say nothing, and take the sect's thanks

effects.log: You take the thanks and the payment and keep your own counsel. A mirror that shows the truth is a dangerous thing to own. Now it is theirs.

events.text: You keep {sr_treasure}, wrapped in three layers of cloth, and still it is warm against your side. You know what it does. Sooner or later you will look into it, and see something, and believe it, because there will be no way not to. You decide not to decide yet.

choices.text: Look into it tonight and be done with it

effects.log: You unwrap it by the fire and look. It shows you one true thing. You sit up until dawn, and in the morning you are steadier.

choices.text: Keep it wrapped until you need it

effects.log: You keep it wrapped. Some day there will be a question only the truth can answer, and you will be ready for it.

events.text: You come out of the Mirror Realm with nothing in your hands. The merchants at the gate look at you and look away. But you know your own face better than you did this morning, and nobody at the gate can say that. It is not the kind of find anyone can steal.

choices.text: Go home and look in an ordinary mirror

effects.log: It is just a mirror. You are just you. It is a strange comfort, how much that is enough.

choices.text: Write down what you learned before it fades

effects.log: It does not fade. You write it anyway. Years later you find the page and it is still true.

events.text: You slip out through a crack in the barrier, and your reflection slips out with you into a puddle on the far side, where it lies looking up at the ordinary sky with an expression of complete astonishment. Then the rain ripples it, and it is only water again, and you are alone and unseen on the road.

choices.text: Walk home by the quiet roads

effects.log: Nobody knows you came out. For a few days you are free of everyone, even yourself.

choices.text: Wait by the puddle a moment

effects.log: It stills again. Your face in it looks lighter than it did. You wave, and it waves back, on time.

events.text: The masked fighters at the gate come at you, and every one of them hesitates for half a heartbeat when they see the shard you carry: in it, each sees their own masked face, and what is under the mask. Half a heartbeat is enough. You cut through, and they scatter, and two of them pull their masks off as they run.

choices.text: Let them go; they have seen enough

effects.log: They have. You watch one of them stop on the hillside, sit down, and put her face in her hands.

choices.text: Hold the shard up for the rest of the crowd

effects.log: Nobody else at the gate tries anything. Nobody else at the gate will look at you, either.

events.text: Masked fighters wait at the gate. When it is done and they have fled, one mask lies cracked on the grass, and the polished inside of it, by some trick of the realm, still holds a reflection: not yours, but the face of the one who wore it, young and frightened, looking up at you from the lining.

choices.text: Lay the mask face down and leave it

effects.log: You leave them their privacy. Whoever they are, they are already having a worse day than you.

choices.text: Keep it, and learn the face

effects.log: You will know them again. They know you will. That is enough of a punishment for some people.

events.text: On the road out, you find that something of the realm came with you. When people lie to you, now, you can see it: a faint silvering of the air around the words, gone in a blink. It is not a gift that makes you popular. It may be the most useful thing you own.

choices.text: Use it gently

effects.log: You let small lies pass and only stop at the big ones. People start to trust you, without knowing why.

choices.text: Use it on everyone

effects.log: Within a week you know three secrets you wish you did not. You are never cheated at market again.
